2026 అక్టోబర్ చివరలో జరిగిన ఇజ్రాయెల్ ఎన్నికల్లో ప్రధానమంత్రి బెంజమిన్ నెతన్యాహు పార్టీ, దాని మిత్రపక్షాలు మొత్తం 53 సీట్లు గెలుచుకున్నాయి. అయితే, ప్రభుత్వాన్ని ఏర్పాటు చేయడానికి అవసరమైన 61 సీట్లను సాధించలేకపోయాయి. ప్రతిపక్ష పార్టీలు 48 సీట్లు గెలుచుకోగా, అరబ్ పార్టీలకు 19 సీట్లు వచ్చాయి. ఎన్నికల తర్వాత, కొత్త ప్రభుత్వాన్ని ఎవరు ఏర్పాటు చేయగలరో నిర్ణయించేందుకు అధ్యక్షుడు ఐజాక్ హెర్జోగ్ వివిధ పార్టీల నాయకులతో చర్చలు ప్రారంభించారు.
ఈ నేపథ్యంలో, ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటులో ముస్లిం ఎంపీలు అందరూ కలిసి నమాజ్ చేస్తున్నారంటూ ఒక వీడియో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) సోషల్ మీడియాలో షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ పోస్టులో చేస్తున్న వాదనలో నిజమెంతుందో ఇప్పుడు పరిశీలిద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటులో ముస్లిం ఎంపీలు అందరూ కలిసి నమాజ్ చేస్తున్న వీడియో.
ఫ్యాక్ట్: ఈ వీడియో జోర్డాన్ రాజధాని అమ్మాన్లోని జోర్డాన్ పార్లమెంటులో 2026 నవంబర్ 3న ఎంపీలు మధ్యాహ్నం (దుహర్) నమాజ్ చేస్తున్న దృశ్యాలను చూపిస్తుంది. ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటులో ముస్లిం ఎంపీలు నమాజ్ చేసినట్లు ఎలాంటి వార్తలు లేవు. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన వాదన తప్పు.
మొదట, ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటు (క్నెసెట్)లో ఇటీవల ఇలాంటి ఘటన ఏదైనా జరిగిందా అని వెతికితే, ఈ ఘటన జరిగినట్టు ఎలాంటి విశ్వసనీయ వార్తా కథనాలు మాకు లభించలేదు. అంతేకాకుండా, ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటు అధికారిక వెబ్సైట్ ప్రకారం, కొత్తగా ఎన్నికైన క్నెసెట్ తొలి సమావేశం 10 నవంబర్ 2026న జరగనుంది. ఈ సమావేశంలో కొత్తగా ఎన్నికైన ఎంపీలు ప్రమాణ స్వీకారం చేయడంతో పాటు, పార్లమెంటు స్పీకర్ను ఎన్నుకోనున్నారు.
తర్వాత, వైరల్ వీడియో యొక్క కీ ఫ్రేమ్లను రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, అవే దృశ్యాలతో కూడిన వీడియోలు BBC News Arabic (ఇక్కడ), జోర్డాన్కు చెందిన మీడియా సంస్థలు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) ప్రచురించినట్లు గుర్తించాం. ఈ కథనాల ప్రకారం, 3 నవంబర్ 2026న జోర్డాన్ రాజధాని అమ్మాన్లోని ప్రతినిధుల సభ (జోర్డాన్ పార్లమెంటు) లో ఎంపీలు మధ్యాహ్నం (దుహర్) నమాజ్ చేస్తున్న దృశ్యాలు ఇవి.
ఈ కథనాల ప్రకారం, పార్లమెంటు శాశ్వత బ్యూరో సభ్యులను ఎన్నుకునేందుకు నిర్ణయించిన సమావేశానికి ముందు ఎంపీ డా. అహ్మద్ అల్-రఖబ్ నమాజ్కు నాయకత్వం వహించారు. కొన్ని మీడియా సంస్థలు ప్రచురించిన పూర్తి వీడియోలో ఆయన నమాజ్కు నాయకత్వం వహిస్తున్న దృశ్యాలను కూడా చూడవచ్చు.
అంతేకాకుండా, వైరల్ వీడియోలో కనిపిస్తున్న జోర్డాన్ జాతీయ చిహ్నం (ఇక్కడ ), అలాగే జోర్డాన్ పార్లమెంటు లోపలి భాగానికి సంబంధించిన దృశ్యాలు (ఇక్కడ) కూడా ఈ వీడియో జోర్డాన్ పార్లమెంటుకు చెందినదేనని స్పష్టం చేస్తున్నాయి.
చివరిగా, జోర్డాన్ పార్లమెంటులో ఎంపీలు నమాజ్ చేస్తున్న వీడియోను, ఇజ్రాయెల్ పార్లమెంటులో ముస్లిం ఎంపీలు నమాజ్ చేస్తున్నారని తప్పుగా షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు.

Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
- Published
Morocco has welcomed the end of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after a diplomatic showdown between the US and Russia left the Security Council unable to agree on its future.
The council failed on Friday to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso) after Russia vetoed a US-backed proposal. A rival Russian draft to extend the mission also failed to secure enough votes.
The decision raises questions about the future of Africa's longest territorial dispute and the fragile ceasefire between Morocco, which claims Western Sahara, and the Polisario Front which has been fighting for the territory's independence for more than 50 years.
Here is what you need to know.
Why is Western Sahara disputed?
Western Sahara, on Africa's north-west coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast.
As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory.
The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination.
Morocco's then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975 about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain.
Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the question of sovereignty.
The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control.
Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario.
Algeria became Polisario's main regional ally, providing military support and hosting its leadership and thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps near the city of Tindouf.
The North African country says its position is based on the right to self-determination, while Morocco sees Western Sahara as an integral part of its territory.
Morocco and Algeria fought a brief border war in 1963 over disagreements about territory inherited from French colonial rule. Their relationship has remained tense, with Western Sahara at the centre of their dispute.
What was the UN's mission role?
After 16 years of fighting, Morocco and Polisario agreed to a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991, with the territory divided by a sand wall, or berm, to keep the rival forces apart.
The UN established Minurso to monitor the ceasefire and organise a referendum on the territory's future. Sahrawis were meant to choose between independence and integration with Morocco.
The vote was scheduled for 1992 but never took place. The two sides could not agree on who would be eligible to participate, with disputes over voter identification becoming a major obstacle.
In 2007, Morocco put forward a proposal for autonomy, which would see Sahrawis managing their internal affairs, while Rabat retained control over defence and foreign relations.
The Polisario Front and Algeria rejected the plan, insisting on a referendum that included independence as an option.
Years of UN-sponsored negotiations failed to produce a breakthrough.
The ceasefire broke down in November 2020, when Polisario said it was resuming armed struggle.
But following a long diplomatic campaign by Morocco, the UN Security Council voted in 2025 in favour of a resolution backing the autonomy plan as the "most feasible" solution for the disputed territory.
While most Sahrawis live in the part of Western Sahara controlled by Morocco, tens of thousands are estimated to be in refugee camps in Algeria.
What happened at the UN?
The US proposed extending Minurso's mandate for another year, but its draft went beyond the usual renewal.
It would have removed the word "referendum" from the mission's name and made Morocco's autonomy proposal the sole basis for further negotiations.
The draft received the support of 11 of the Security Council's 15 members, including France and the UK but Russia vetoed it, arguing that it was too favourable to Morocco.
Russia then proposed extending Minurso's mandate without changing its terms. That draft also failed, receiving only two votes in favour.
Minurso's mandate expired at the end of Saturday, 31 October. The UN said the following day that the mission had entered a liquidation period, with a reduced team overseeing the transfer of military equipment and other assets.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination must be respected and warned of the risk of renewed hostilities.
The Polisario Front condemned the US proposal. Its representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing it, saying it would "torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process" and threaten regional and international peace.
Morocco, meanwhile, said the mission's personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days, arguing that Western Sahara issue should no longer be considered by the Security Council.
Minurso had 155 military personnel and was expected to cost $62m (£46m) in the financial year beginning in June, according to a UN report.
Why is Morocco celebrating the end of the UN mission?
Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso's mandate.
In Laayoune, the territory's largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI.
"The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute," Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC.
He said Morocco would now have more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence towards autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.
The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara's legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.
Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).
But the decision comes after several countries backed the position of Morocco, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim a central part of its foreign policy.
In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.
France also backed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute in 2024.
Morocco rejoined the African Union in 2017, more than three decades after leaving its predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in protest at the SADR's admission.
Since returning, Rabat has sought to build support for its position from within the organisation. At least 10 African countries have opened diplomatic missions in the territory in support of Rabat.
"Morocco is not necessarily seeking to abandon the UN process, but to change the framework for negotiations and draw greater support from regional organisations," says Laaroussi.
Addressing a special joint session of parliament on Monday, House of Representatives Speaker Ahmed Touizi hailed the end of Minurso as a victory for the country's diplomacy.
He said the country should now move from "managing the dispute to implementing its autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty, while pressing ahead with development projects in the territory."
Could this lead to a renewed war?
The fear is that Minurso's departure could lead to renewed fighting.
The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation.
Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians.
Laaroussi admits that the mission's departure could create security gaps.
"Minurso's departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment," he says.
The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online.
Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara.
In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country's claim to sovereignty over the territory.
Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it "within respect of its security and sovereignty."
Polisario has not said what it will do next.
Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high.
According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver.
Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco's $6.3bn.

If you've been coveting one of Rocco’s smart designer minifridges, you might be interested to know the brand's biggest sale of 2026 starts today, featuring the brand-new Rocco Essential for under $1,000 and the OG Classic in this year’s new Beige colorway, as well as white and two rare blue colors, for $1,495—as low as the Classic ever gets.
Today also marks the rerelease of the Classic's Icy Blue and Royal Blue, two rarely seen colors that Rocco says are not coming back after this year.
The Essential
The Essential was just released in August and just began shipping in September; I'm currently testing it now. It's only been about a week and a half, but early impressions are positive. It has the same smart sight system as the Classic, but the biggest difference is obviously the look. Vintage-inspired fluted glass and rounded edges are out; sleek minimalism is in. The tinted dark glass door takes up the entire front, with a color-matched metal handle you can swap out for midcentury-inspired oak for an extra $95.
It's only got one temperature zone as opposed to the Classic's two, but my favorite part so far has been the interior—instead of the Classic's old-fashioned wire racks, the Essential sports smooth-glide drawers lined with a rubbery material and grip strips. This makes it much more accommodating to oddly shaped drinks, and prevents cans (it can hold up to 77) from rolling around every time you open your Rocco. It also gets colder than the Classic model—down to 34 degrees Fahrenheit instead of 37. My main frustration so far is that the sight system has been a little spotty and slow to recognize when drinks have been removed, but I'm having that problem with the Classic as well, so it's not specific to this model. All colors (Cream, Sage, Graphite) of the Essential are currently discounted.
The Classic
The handsome, vintage-inspired model is the one that started it all. Its thick steel body comes in a range of fun colors, the fluted glass refracts potentially drink-damaging light, and it comes with a color-matched metal tray so it can double as a bar cart. It's got two isolated temperature zones for red and white wine (or extra-crispy Cokes), plus five full-sized racks and one half-rack—enough for 88 cans or 27 bottles of wine. The wire racks don't pull out as smoothly as the Essential's rubber-lined drawers, but this is otherwise a top-of-the-line beverage cooler with an impressive 10-year warranty.
You can also control the interior lights from your phone. The sight system, however, is buggy—my Classic is currently displaying a rack of Dr. Pepper and Stella Artois bottles I had left over from a party in July (they were consumed not long after that), so I would not recommend buying one of these for the sight system alone. (Note this sale is on the Beige, White, Royal Blue, and Icy Blue Classic only.)
Back in Blue
I’m partial to the Classic’s forest green, but even I've got to admit the blue hues look pretty good. They sold out almost immediately around this time last year, so if you've been wanting one and you see this, I wouldn't wait to add it to your cart.

Godzilla is once again proving to be a formidable box-office force, with the latest installment in the long-running kaijū (monster) franchise setting records in Japan before making a powerful debut abroad.
“Godzilla Minus Zero,” directed by Takashi Yamazaki, opened in Japan on Nov. 3 — Japan’s designated “Godzilla Day” in honor of when the original “Godzilla” debuted in Japanese theaters in 1954 — earning ¥910 million ($5.75 million) and attracting more than 590,000 moviegoers on its first day.
According to the film’s official X account, the opening-day takings marked the highest single-day box office revenue for a live-action film in Japanese history. A subsequent post announced that domestic attendance had passed 1 million within four days of release.
The sequel to 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” continued its strong run overseas, opening in 3,254 North American theaters on Friday and grossing $14.5 million on opening day, taking the top spot in the daily box-office rankings.
It went on to gross $31.6 million over its opening weekend, making it the biggest debut to date for distributor Gkids and the strongest opening for a live-action foreign-language film since 2004’s “Hero.”
“Godzilla Minus Zero” is the first Japanese feature shot for IMAX screens, and it has brought in $21.3 million worldwide through Sunday from IMAX screens alone.
It recently screened at the Tokyo International Film Festival, which wrapped on Wednesday, as the event’s centerpiece film.
Its predecessor, “Godzilla Minus One,” earned roughly $105.4 million worldwide and became the highest grossing Japanese-language live-action film ever released in North America. It also made history as the first Japanese film to win the Academy Award for best visual effects at the 96th Academy Awards in 2024.
“When we were making ‘Minus One,’ going overseas wasn’t even a consideration, and it ended up reaching so many people,” Yamazaki, who also handled the screenplay and visual effects for both films, told The Japan Times in a recent interview. “Making something rooted in home isn’t the opposite of making something for the world.
“If we tried to imitate Hollywood, there’d be no point. Not thinking about overseas audiences is, paradoxically, how we think about them. That’s the only way Japanese films can really travel.”

The 2026 festive season began in muted fashion, but the performance of some of the key new-age tech stocks in the pre-festive quarter (Q2 FY27) shows that even in this environment businesses are able to extract and expand profits, and grow their topline. When we see the financial performance of ecommerce, fintech and logistics stocks, it’s clear companies entered this period with a lot more confidence and absorbed some of these headwinds. Pretty much each one of them improved on their profitability metrics and their topline. As Inc42 reported in October, early data from the festive season sales indicated that Indian consumers kept shopping, but with more abandon. Online sales slipped from last year, card spending and smartphone sales weakened, and surveys suggest urban households are trimming discretionary budgets too. Rising household costs, uncertainty over jobs and incomes, and discounts that no longer feel compelling have made shoppers wary of big-ticket purchases. Consumers are still browsing for products, but in the current climate, conversion rates have fallen for premium products, which usually see a big uptick. A lot of this has to do with the macroeconomic factors, rising energy prices and logistics costs, and lingering grave geopolitical concerns that have dented consumer confidence and spending. In Q2, logistics tech players expanded capacity ahead of the festive shopping rush, with higher volumes offering an opportunity to improve operating leverage. Ecommerce companies capitalised on seasonal demand, even as the pressure to balance growth with profitability persisted. Meanwhile, fintech companies, particularly those with a big UPI focus, faced a different equation: the prospect of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions. While MDR itself is yet to come into effect, the fintech ecosystem’s quarter was defined by swelling toplines, which bodes well for the next quarter where MDR is likely to become a real factor. Profitability broadened across the listed new-age tech universe, with nine of the 11 large tech stocks (with a market cap of over ₹10,000 Cr) across these key sectors reporting a net profit in Q2 FY27. The combined bottomline of these companies improved by around ₹1,100–1,400 Cr year-on-year (YoY), depending on how exceptional items in the base quarter are treated, according to market data. More importantly, EBITDA grew faster than revenue at all nine profitable companies, suggesting that operating leverage is beginning to show up in reported performance. But a significant profit pool remained concentrated in a handful of companies, while businesses such as Swiggy and Meesho continue to report losses despite improving operating metrics. Atul Thakkar, executive director at Anand Rathi Investment Banking, believes the market is moving towards rewarding earnings delivery rather than growth narratives. “Over the next 12–18 months, we expect earnings delivery, rather than growth narratives, to be the main driver of returns in this space,” he said, This distinction is particularly relevant when the three major segments, fintech, logistics and ecommerce are assessed separately. Fintech has delivered the strongest operating performance, logistics has shown some of the clearest margin improvement, and ecommerce has produced a wide range of outcomes. But how did the profitability story unfolded across these three sectors? Logistics Tech Shifts Into High Gear It was largely a capacity-building quarter for logistics companies, with the full benefit of festive demand expected to play out in Q3. Yet, the results already point to improving operating leverage, as shipment volumes grew faster than revenue at the larger third-party logistics (3PL) players. Shadowfax’s revenue rose 57%, while express and hyperlocal orders grew nearly 70%. Adjusted EBITDA increased sharply, with margins expanding to 5%. Delhivery reported a similar divergence: express shipments grew 32%, against 22% growth in express revenue. Its adjusted EBITDA margin also improved, while first-half operating cash flow more than doubled. The gap between volume and revenue growth suggests that incremental shipments are not translating into proportionate revenue. Profitability, therefore, will depend on whether higher volumes can offset pricing pressure and rising costs across fuel, wages and last-mile delivery. Delhivery’s return to profitability also needs context: the year-ago quarter included acquisition-related integration costs linked to Ecom Express. Its adjusted EBITDA and cash generation offer a more useful measure of underlying progress. Shiprocket, meanwhile, turned profitable, reporting a net profit of ₹60 Lakh against a loss of ₹20.3 Cr a year ago. Revenue grew 35%, while adjusted EBITDA more than tripled. Its core business continued to expand, with transactions growing 31% and adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 12.8%. The results point to improving economics, although the reported profit remains modest. Across the sector, technology and network utilisation are central to the margin story. Shadowfax is deploying AI-led route optimisation and expanding its seller platform, while Delhivery is investing in automation and autonomous material-handling systems. These initiatives could improve productivity, but their returns will depend on execution and the ability to absorb peak-season volumes without adding costs at the same pace. The festive quarter will be the real test. Stronger volumes should support operating leverage, but sustained margin expansion will require better network utilisation, disciplined pricing and control over fulfilment costs. Logistics is showing clearer signs of improving economics, though the gap between shipment growth and revenue realisation remains a key risk. Fintech’s Profit Engines Roar Fintech was the strongest performer in Q2 FY27, with all the major companies in the segment reporting profits. Moreover, EBITDA growth outpaced revenue growth at each, pointing to improving operating leverage. The gains, however, are coming from deeper monetisation of existing customers rather than payment volumes alone. Paytm is increasingly diversifying beyond payments, with financial services distribution contributing about a third of its revenue. Its merchant subscription base and financial services business continue to expand, reducing its dependence on payment processing. Meanwhile, Pine Labs is extracting more value from its merchant network through subscriptions, affordability products and transaction-linked services. PB Fintech’s growing renewal book offers a similar advantage: recurring insurance revenue is expanding faster than its core insurance business, making growth less dependent on fresh policy acquisition. The bigger question for fintech is whether these operating gains can withstand regulatory changes. The proposed UPI MDR framework could create an additional revenue stream, but the benefit to payment companies will depend on how the pool is shared between banks and other ecosystem participants. With implementation postponed beyond the festive period, it remains an opportunity rather than an earnings driver for now. Insurance distribution faces a more direct overhang. The proposed changes to commission structures and expense limits could alter the economics of online intermediaries such as PB Fintech. Its growing renewal revenue offers some cushion, but the impact on new-policy distribution remains uncertain. “While fintech companies have demonstrated an ability to improve monetisation and operating leverage, the regulatory environment remains a key determinant of how sustainable these gains will be. For this segment, regulation is a bigger variable than execution,” said Thakkar. Ecommerce’s Profitability Divide Widens Ecommerce delivered the widest divergence in Q2 FY27. While revenue growth remained strong across quick commerce, ecommerce and consumer brands, profitability varied sharply, reflecting differences in scale, cost structures and monetisation. For example, Meesho saw its net loss narrow to 68%, while marketplace contribution margin improved to 6% of NMV from 3.3% a year ago. However, newer initiatives remain loss-making and are yet to establish meaningful scale. Consumer brands delivered a more consistent earnings performance. Nykaa’s profit more than tripled, supported by margin expansion and growth across beauty and fashion. Lenskart also reported strong profit growth, with expansion across its India and international businesses. Higher store productivity, rising volumes and operating cash flow suggest that growth is being supported by better utilisation of the existing network, alongside store additions. Input-cost inflation remains another pressure point for consumer brands. Passing on higher costs through pricing could protect margins but risks weighing on demand and average order values. Gross margins, customer retention and acquisition costs will be as important as revenue growth in assessing the durability of earnings. Why Profits Are Just Half The Story As these sectors continue to mature, operating leverage is becoming more important than headline growth. However, profitability remains concentrated, with a handful of companies accounting for a substantial share of the sector’s earnings. The ownership shift is also worth watching. Foreign investors have reduced exposure to several listed new-age tech companies, while domestic institutions have increased participation. But domestic ownership is no guarantee against corrections when earnings or regulatory developments disappoint. According to market analysts, retail investors are likely to increasingly favour companies that are not only profitable but also generate revenue from multiple products within their existing customer base and use operating cash flow to fund expansion. We can see this in the aggressive diversification across the industry, particularly in fintech and logistics tech. This wave favours established fintech businesses, asset-light logistics networks and ecommerce companies where the seller-customer flywheel is up and running. Post the festive season spike, even if it may be a relatively smaller spike compared to previous years, the cash generation and regulatory resilience of these companies will be worth watching. That could very well mark the next phase of maturity. But can these growth levers convince public market investors to look beyond its thin margins? Honasa’s Profit Up 87%: The Mamaearth parent reported an 87% YoY jump in Q2 FY27 net profit to ₹73.2 Cr, while revenue rose 36% to ₹731.2 Cr. Growth across focus categories, offline channels and younger brands helped drive the company’s quarterly performance. Go Digit PAT Dips: Go Digit’s net profit declined 31.1% YoY to ₹142.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 despite a marginal 1.7% rise in insurance revenue to ₹2,720.5 Cr. Higher insurance service expenses and claims weighed on profitability, even as motor insurance revenue grew. RateGain Profit Rises 47%:The travel-focused SaaS company’s profit rose 46.5% YoY to ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, driven by operating revenue zooming 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr. This came on the back of the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, which RateGain acquired for $250 Mn last year. Moneyview Revenue Grows 41%: The fintech company’s consolidated net profit surged 417.6% YoY to ₹200.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue grew 41% to ₹1,120.2 Cr. The fintech reported a managed AUM of ₹23,892 Cr, with its shares gaining 5.7% following the earnings announcement.

Before Attempting SD Card Recovery
Before performing a recovery of your SD card, here are a few methods that you can follow to improve the chances of recovering your lost files on your SD card:
First, don’t copy new photos or record new videos on this SD card. This prevents new data from being written to the memory card. Also, don’t transfer new files to the affected card. If needed, use a different SD card, especially if you are in the middle of recording or need to transfer your files quickly.
Next, do not format or initialize the memory card, even if the device you connected to asks you to. This also includes repair solutions commonly offered by devices such as PCs to recover your memory card; we strongly recommend avoiding them, as they can change the stored data.
Finally, before attempting recovery, make sure your missing files aren’t already saved somewhere else. Check your camera memory cards, your computer import folders, and any external hard drives or backups to confirm. If you find copies, open the files to confirm they work as expected so you don’t have to recover them again.
Finally, check the condition of your SD card. In general, recovery software works best when the computer detects the SD card and the connection stays stable throughout the recovery process. You can also recover files even if they won’t open.

What if a Recovered Video Won’t Play?
If some of your recovered videos won’t play, there are many possible reasons. The most common reason is that interrupted video recordings can become corrupted, since video recovery is more complicated than recovering deleted photos.
This happens especially when video data or structured information is missing. Remember, recovering a video file doesn’t always guarantee it will play. Make sure the entire scan and repair process finishes without issues, then review the videos after processing. This is one of the best things about Recoverit’s 15 video repair functionality, as it helps you recover even damaged videos, even when the process is more complicated than photo recovery.
Still, keep in mind that if the necessary data has already been lost or overwritten, the repair function cannot guarantee recovery, and restoration may be impossible. Also, unlike regular recordings, data from drones and action cameras requires extra attention. We highly recommend keeping the original recorded video and examining the repaired version separately.
Final Thoughts
Recoverit 15 can help you recover photos and videos lost from an SD card; in particular, its video repair functionality can help repair damaged clips. If you still have questions, we have answered most frequently asked questions below.
Frequently Asked Questions
1. Can Deleted Files Be Recovered from the Memory Card?
Yes, as long as your card is still recognized, you may be able to recover deleted files, but you need to ensure the memory card is readable and the data hasn’t been overwritten.
2. Can Recoverit Recover RAW Photos and Camera Video Files?
Yes, Recoverit supports recovering various photo, video, and camera file formats from memory cards, including RAW images and different wide formats. However, results may depend on the file’s condition and supported formats.
3. What if a Recovered Video or Photo Still Won’t Open?
The recovered file may still be damaged, fragmented, or corrupted, preventing it from opening. In such cases, you can use file recovery and file repair services separately and try repairing the file after recovery.
4. Can Overwritten Files Be Recovered?
No, overwritten files are generally not recoverable because a new file replaces the deleted file’s data. That’s why we highly recommend stopping use of the SD card as soon as you notice the missing content and starting your recovery process immediately. And once you have successfully recovered files using software like Recoverit, there are a few steps we would like to recommend to prevent future data loss:
- Verify the recovered files and back up the recovered data immediately.
- Maintain two copies in two different storage locations.
- Verify the data completely before formatting your memory card.
- If the memory card has an issue, we highly recommend replacing it with a newer one, since you still risk losing data on future shoots.

Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran. The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses. Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.
Rainfall exceeded forecasts, with an estimated 80mm falling in the city, compared with expectations of 30mm. Two people were killed in the floods.
In Europe, Storm Bruna is forecast to bring strong winds to Portugal this week, particularly along the west coast. Gusts are expected to reach 50mph (80km/h), with heavy rain and thunderstorms also expected. The total rainfall could reach 200mm by the end of the week. The storm has already affected the Canary Islands, where Tenerife recorded a gust of 80mph on Saturday night.
Japan experienced a cold and snowy end to last week, with further snowfall expected in Hokkaido and parts of the mountains in the main island Honshu.
Temperatures in Japan are forecast to fall below the seasonal average early this week, with Sapporo, the capital of Hokkaido prefecture, expected to plunge to 10C below average. Maximum temperatures in the city are likely to be about 4-6C on Monday and Wednesday, while Tuesday’s high is forecast to be about 0C. Minimum temperatures could fall to -6C by Wednesday, and -8C in other western parts of Hokkaido on Tuesday.
Ski resorts are preparing for visitors after snowfall began on Friday. Total snowfall is expected to reach 30-50cm around Kiroro and Niesko, with about 20-30cm in Furano, Rusutsu and Sapporo.
Other resorts could receive up to 20cm of snow by Wednesday. Strong winds accompanied the snow on Friday and over the weekend, with gusts of about 75mph in Kiroko and Niesko.
During the strong El Niño, sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific were about 3.5C above the climatological average at their peak in late October. The story behind seven remasters
In a lengthy blog post published this week, Jim Vessella, a senior producer at EA, described the efforts that went into remastering Wing Commander I-IV and Prophecy, Privateer 2, and Road Rash.
It’s a long, detailed story that’s worth reading yourself, but here’s a top-level summary. After working on the mostly widely acclaimed Command & Conquer: Remastered Collection in 2019, Vessella writes that he learned about and visited a room at EA’s Redwood Shores campus that contained a large archive of poorly labeled or sorted physical media from ages past.
In his free time, and with the help of others, he began cataloging this archive and discovered, among other things, that it contained virtually the entirety of the original masters of Wing Commander III and Wing Commander IV‘s full-motion-video cutscenes.

Desperate families flee hometowns as shuttered schools leave students packed in crowded classrooms
Across the U.S., many students are experiencing disruptions as school buildings close and consolidate due to declining enrollment and reduced funding

Thousands of American students began this academic year at unfamiliar schools after their campuses were shut down.
Starting a new school year can be nerve-wracking under any circumstances, but for these pupils, it came with the added challenge of adjusting to an entirely new school after their previous ones closed.
An increasing number of cash-strapped school districts around the country have resorted to closing campuses to save money, as U.S. birth rates continue a multidecade slide and state and federal education funding dries up.
New research shows student enrollment has fallen much faster than schools are closing, suggesting more painful financial choices lie ahead. The Associated Press is covering school closures in partnership with The Hechinger Report and Big Local News at Stanford University. These are some takeaways from their reporting.
A total of 1,156 U.S. schools closed during the last academic year, the highest number since the pandemic, according to an analysis of federal data by Big Local News at Stanford University. The Vallejo City Unified School District, a working-class district near San Francisco, serves half as many students as it did two decades earlier.
District leaders have closed five campuses since 2025, a quarter of the district's schools. They've also placed up to a third of all staff positions on the chopping block to help plug a staggering $36 million deficit. In Vallejo, a city still struggling to bounce back from the closure of a naval base in the 1990s, school enrollment has tumbled from nearly 18,000 in the fall of 2006 to about 9,300, the district says.
School districts nationwide, including large systems in Cleveland, Houston and Philadelphia, are facing similar closures. The enrollment and financial situation is unlikely to improve, said Lydia Rainey, research principal at the Center on Reinventing Public Education.
“States aren’t about to open the coffers and swoop in with additional funds to save schools,” she said. Nationwide, public school enrollment fell by more than 1.4 million students, roughly 3%, between fall 2019 and 2024, according to an Associated Press analysis of federal education data collected by Stanford University economist Thomas Dee and sociologist Jaymes Pyne.
The total number of schools has declined, too, but only to about pre-pandemic levels, the researchers found, suggesting closures are lagging behind enrollment declines. Lower birth rates are the primary reason for enrollment decline, but a federal crackdown on immigration and the post-pandemic expansion of private school vouchers and homeschool options have contributed.
Bellwether and WestEd, two research groups, recently estimated declining enrollment could cause schools to lose $11.5 billion in state revenue annually by 2030-2031, potentially prompting widespread layoffs, cuts to academic programs and school closures. Research shows closing schools rarely yields the financial relief districts hope for.
Busing students to their reassigned schools, severance for pink-slipped staff and security for empty facilities often eat up any savings. School closures can also set students back academically and make it harder to attract teachers, who may worry the jobs aren't stable. Closing schools can trigger a downward spiral, too, as frustrated families flee to charter or private schools or other districts.
In Vallejo, some parents said they chose to homeschool this fall or were planning to sell their homes and move to neighboring districts. “Families are literally packing up their kids and moving away,” said Vallejo mom Kimberly Núñez-Brandão, whose daughter's elementary school closed.
She recently attended curriculum night for her daughter's new school, Glen Cove Elementary, and shared her shock at learning Penny's new fifth-grade teacher had 32 students in his first class. “They already overwhelmed teachers with 30-plus students,” she said.
“Who’s winning here?” Rubén Aurelio, superintendent for Vallejo schools, acknowledged cuts and closures can be hard for families but said they are necessary to correct for school districts and budgets designed for a different reality.
“We’re not just closing schools to close schools,” Aurelio said. “We’re right-sizing a district that was built for significantly more kids. And if we’re going to actually improve outcomes for the kids we still have, we need to concentrate resources.”
The already painful cost-cutting measure may push even more families into competing charter networks, neighboring districts or private alternatives, further eroding the funding schools get per enrolled student. So along with cutting budgets, Vallejo is renovating older campuses, hoping to draw younger parents who can't afford to start a family in San Francisco.
The superintendent said he also plans to open a Tagalog-language school soon, targeting Filipino families from across the Bay Area. Marisa de la Torre, a managing director of the UChicago Consortium on School Research, said instability created by school closures may last for a while. Studies from the University of Chicago show that academically, displaced students often suffer long-term drops in reading and math.
That's especially true when students end up at low-performing schools. “It takes a while to recover, if they recover at all,” she said. Núñez-Brandão isn't sure she wants to stick around long enough to find out. Weeks into the new school year, Penny still struggled to adjust to Glen Cove.
She started to make new friends and said she feels comfortable on campus. She also liked her teacher, a first-year educator who'd joined Vallejo's teacher residency program, launched last year to attract new educators and improve retention. But with 32 kids in the class, she said it's hard to concentrate.
On a Tuesday in October, Núñez-Brandão received a note in the Glen Cove parent portal: Penny's teacher resigned, effective immediately. The school will rely on a long-term substitute for now, the district said. The Associated Press' education coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations.

With rolling heat waves sweeping the globe, 2027 is shaping up to be the hottest year on record. As the health risks of extreme temperatures mount, there's never been a better time to rethink sustainable cooling.
Air conditioners and electric fans account for around 20 percent of electricity used in buildings worldwide—3 to 4 percent of total greenhouse gas emissions—and, as demand for cooling in homes, workplaces, and schools grows, the number of AC units in use could reach 5.5 billion by 2050.
The solution isn't one magic fix, but a suite of emerging technologies heading for living rooms and apartment windows. From radar sensors tracking your body to compact heat pumps and climate-safe refrigerants, here is how the next generation of air-conditioning plans to keep us cool without cooking the planet.
The “Intelligent AC” Boom
In 1994, Mitsubishi Electric was zooming past the air-con competition, introducing the first motion and occupancy sensors for AC, with infrared 3D sensing eventually following in the mid-2010s. Fast-forward to 2026 and AI-powered ACs now track people in the home with millimeter-level precision.
AC makers have launched intelligent, targeted air conditioner units all year, from Samsung’s Bespoke AI system in March to Dyson’s Find+Follow feature for its Purifier Cool fan in June. At IFA in September, we got a whole sweep from Chinese companies like Hisense, Dreo, and Midea.
LG’s latest DualCool AI AC has a 5-meter radar sensor for people detection plus targeting based on your everyday movement patterns. Hisense’s Companion Living AC also uses data from smart home sensors to identify and precool “target paths” within the home, based on your routines. So if you always head from the couch to the kitchen for a midnight snack, your AC can cool that particular zone before you even get up.
The real-time cooling features aim to improve comfort inside sticky homes. A secondary benefit is that precisely locating people and delivering cooling directly to them could reduce energy consumption. “It definitely has the potential to reduce the total energy use for air-conditioning,” says Björn Palm, senior professor in energy technology at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm. By how much? That's less clear.
Dyson’s Find+Follow purifier and fan uses a simple, low-resolution camera, feeding the “stick figure”-like, anonymous coordinates of its 17-point person detection into an algorithm, all instantly processed on-device and deleted, without any face recognition. “It can tell that you’re a human, whether you’re sitting or standing, which direction you’re moving," says Alex Hudson, an environmental care engineer at Dyson. "It might map your arms and shoulders.”
The Purifier Cool can oscillate 350 degrees between “up to six people” in the space, directing airflow for personalized cooling. One hour after it detects that everyone has left the room, the appliance will switch to Auto mode and—if there is no big pollution spike for the purifier to deal with, like a truck driving past an open window—it’s a "considerably lower power draw than when it’s in fan mode, so there’s definitely a benefit there,” Hudson says.
Samsung’s Bespoke AI WindFree Pro adds a motion radar sensor, which can recognize and track two occupants. “AI Direct Wind” can follow and blast you for immediate cooling, whereas “AI Indirect Wind,” you guessed it, cools the spot you’re in without blowing air right in your face. Samsung’s residential environment tests claim energy savings of “up to 30 percent” with its overall AI energy mode switched on. At IFA, Samsung added wearable data: a Galaxy Watch or Galaxy Ring can signal to the AC when you’ve fallen asleep, triggering a gentler Windfree Cooling mode overnight.
Midea’s VitaBreeze AC, launching in early 2027, combines user photos with millimeter-wave radar sensors to personalize cooling. During setup, the user manually uploads a series of room images to the app, indicating the air conditioner placement. The AC then uses those images with radar data to create a 3D virtual grid of the room and furniture position.
Millimeter wave (or mmWave) radar—the kind used in 5G cellular technology—bounces short-wavelength radio waves, typically 1 to 10 millimeters, to detect an object's distance and angle, as well as tiny movements in real time. Here, the Midea app’s Follow Me feature, similar to Samsung's, can pinpoint your real-time position in the room, triggering louver adjustments as you move around. Manuel Seethaler, head of Midea's Residential Air Conditioning product strategy in Europe, says that its technology can save more than 30 percent of energy in cooling mode compared with units without these algorithms.
The average AC sold in 2024 was already about 20 percent more efficient than an equivalent model in 2014. However, there’s still plenty of room to grow, as the IEA predicts that “cooling demand” will grow by 1,600 terawatt-hours by 2035—Japan and South Korea’s total electricity combined. But this kind of proximity sensing could also result in marginal energy savings.
“There is a performance improvement you can get if [targeted AC] is done well,” says Vincent Romanin, founder and CTO of San Francisco–based Gradient, which makes 120-volt all-weather window AC/heat pumps. “But we’re going into buildings where we’re reducing the energy by 85 percent and to design another feature that gets us to 87 percent? I personally have never used a product with an occupancy sensor that I feel like worked well.”
Compact Window ACs
For Palm, to reach sustainable home cooling by 2050, we need three major changes: cheaper, compact heat pumps for all home sizes; fewer toxic natural refrigerants (fluids and chemical compounds that absorb and release heat); and newly designed systems with low charge to ensure safety.
Heat pumps have become a modern, efficient option for heating and cooling. For heating, it's a four-stage process: absorbing outside heat to produce gas via a refrigerant; compressing to raise the temperature; condensing, where heat is passed to the water in your home’s heating system; and cooling back into a liquid via an expansion valve to drop the pressure. When cooling is needed, the reversing valve switches back to run the process from inside to outside for air-conditioning.
The key is to persuade renters and people living in smaller homes to make the overall switch. “For the domestic market, we need heat pumps which fit into an apartment without being too noisy or bulky,” Palm says. It's also critical to reduce the price.
Gradient units typically use one-third less energy than a standard window AC, mostly for heating but with cooling efficiencies too. They’re a quick self-install option that lets apartment renters get their window back, see lower bills, and run a quieter AC system than older models.
But fixing the form factor only solves part of the equation. Palm’s other criteria—replacing toxic synthetic refrigerants with natural alternatives like propane (R290), as in Bosch's Climate 6000iP, which launched in September—present a tougher engineering challenge. Leaking refrigerants alone account for an estimated 720 million metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions every year. Natural refrigerants dramatically curb the potential for global warming, but their flammability demands complex, spark-free redesigns and low-charge systems that US regulators and supply chains are still cautious about embracing.
Reaching sustainable cooling by 2050 won’t be glamorous, Palm says. Ultimately, the future of home cooling won't hinge on an air conditioner that tracks you to the kitchen for a midnight snack—it depends on the unsexy, invisible mechanical work happening deep inside the compressor.

England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting.

The ramifications of the Argentina defeat, or perhaps more pertinently, the circumstances, meant some of the squad held grievances, with those feelings lingering and even growing throughout the summer.

Enzo Fernandez struck an equaliser with five minutes left, before Lautaro Martinez headed in a stoppage-time winner.
As reported by BBC Sport at the time, a number of senior England players held misgivings at Tuchel's instructions for the closing stages of the Argentina loss, believing the approach was too negative and defensive.

What was said at the review meeting
Inevitably, the game against Argentina emerged as a key theme at the squad discussion.
It is understood that Tuchel pointed to the quality of the opposition as a key factor on why they eventually succumbed to two late Argentina goals.
There is, of course, merit to that argument. Lionel Messi was in the opposition team after all.
That said, it was not an argument the players in the meeting were prepared to universally accept.
There is a strongly held view within the England squad that their team, man-for-man, was superior to Argentina, who had 38-year-old Nicolas Otamendi on the field for the closing 18 minutes of the game.

"I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways."
We will get a clearer idea of how 'Tuchel 2.0' is progressing in the next few days when England host Croatia on Thursday and travel to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday.

From Chanel 2.55 to Lady Dior: Why quilted bags remain fashion icons 70 years on
From Chanel’s iconic 2.55 to today’s oversized, pillowy designs, quilting has evolved beyond its classic diamond stitches into one of fashion’s most recognisable handbag signatures.
The most intriguing handbag at Chanel's Spring/Summer 2027 show last month wasn't new. It was Gabrielle Chanel's own 2.55, borrowed from the house's patrimoine (French for heritage) archives and carried by model Dyanira Hurbuscher, who opened and closed Matthieu Blazy's show with the historic piece.
First launched in February 1955 (hence its name), the 2.55 introduced design details that continue to inspire even today.
Take its soldiers' bag-inspired shoulder strap, for instance, which allowed women to go hands-free at a time when clutches and top-handle bags were the norm.
Then there was the quilting. Inspired by Chanel's love of horse riding and equestrian coats and covers, the diamond pattern would become one of the house's most recognisable signatures. More than 70 years later, it remains a visual shorthand for luxury, even as other designers have taken quilting in directions Chanel might never have imagined.
THE SHAPE OF THINGS
What quilting actually looks like on a bag, however, comes down to more than the stitches you can see. Much of its shape and texture, unsurprisingly, depends on what lies beneath them.
Softer leathers and generous padding create fuller, rounder surfaces, while firmer materials keep the lines cleaner and more controlled. Meanwhile, synthetics like nylon and polyester can take quilting in a lighter, sportier direction.
Thus, two bags can share the same quilted pattern and still look – and feel – almost nothing alike.
HOUSE STYLE
Quilting was hardly Chanel's alone, of course, and other houses developed their own recognisable geometric signatures. Dior's cannage, for instance, took inspiration from something less obvious than a handbag archive: chairs.
The Napoleon III-style seats used at 30 Avenue Montaigne featured a lattice of squares crossed by diagonals, giving cannage a more rigid, architectural quality than Chanel's softer diamond grid. The motif would go on to appear on perfume bottles, tweed and, fittingly, the Lady Dior, introduced in 1995.
Miu Miu's matelasse, meanwhile, takes quilting in a more gathered, almost ruched direction – an example of a house developing a signature texture that can be recognised almost as quickly as its logo.
Seen on the Coffer bag from Miuccia Prada's Fall/Winter 2006 era, the technique gives leather a puckered, rippling surface that looks more gathered than stitched.
Since then, it has appeared on bags including the Wander and Arcadie, changing in scale and colour while remaining distinctly Miu Miu.
By contrast, Saint Laurent's 2017 LouLou by Anthony Vaccarello replaced quilting's familiar diamonds with Vs in a chevron pattern, giving an otherwise soft and feminine flap bag a little more backbone.
Marc Jacobs' Stam, which emerged from his Fall/Winter 2005 era and has since been revived, took a different approach. Its quilted leather, ladylike shape and chunky hardware gave it the slightly retro, slightly excessive charm that made it a Noughties favourite – and a fitting candidate for a comeback.
PUFF PIECES
If heritage houses used quilting to establish recognisable signatures, a newer wave of designers began playing with the padding itself, exaggerating its proportions to sometimes almost comical effect.
At Bottega Veneta, Daniel Lee's Padded Cassette turned the house's familiar woven geometry into thick, rounded panels, making the bag look almost cushioned. Louis Vuitton's 2022 Bubblegram collection did something similar with its Monogram, using embroidery and padding to give the familiar motif a softer, cloud-like finish.
Cos, too, played with inflation. Its 2021 quilted bag, made from recycled polyester and popularised after Blackpink's Jennie carried one, became enough of a phenomenon to rank as the third-hottest product in Lyst's Q3 2023 Index.
The fast-selling style even picked up the unofficial nickname "the Jennie bag" – despite looking nothing like the polished leather flap bags that had defined quilted handbags for decades.
And yet, for all these reinventions, the classic diamond quilt still carries a particular association with luxury. Part of it comes from the pattern itself: the repeated geometry gives padded leather depth and structure without letting it look too soft or shapeless. The rest can be chalked up to cultural memory.
Quilting may now come gathered, chevroned, oversized or puffed up enough to resemble upholstery, but more than 70 years of Chanel being Chanel have trained us to see a diamond quilt and think luxury before we've even registered a logo.
Chances are, too, that we'll be reminded of the original 2.55.

You can run AI models locally on Android and iPhone using Google AI Edge Gallery or PocketPal AI, and on Mac and Windows using LM Studio or Ollama. Simply install the app, download a compatible AI model, and start using it offline. Your data stays on your device, with no cloud access required after setup.
While many think AI is a bubble that is going to burst one day, it might be true, or it might not be at all. Only time will tell. But we should all accept that AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with our devices and do work.
For me, my life revolves around AI: I hand off some of my work to it and do things that once weren’t possible.
AI models are rapidly evolving. If you don’t know what an AI model is, it powers the apps and interfaces you interact with. For instance, the ChatGPT app uses GPT models, and the Claude app is powered by Claude models, which run behind the scenes.
While AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with devices and making work easier, handing your sensitive data to it has remained a major privacy concern.But thanks to rapid AI model development, many capable, powerful AI models enough to run locally on your device, without your data leaving your device
Companies like Google and Meta offer free AI models that can run locally on most consumer devices, including your mobile phone. Apps like Google’s AI Edge Gallery and PocketPal AI also make it easy to discover and run AI models locally without technical expertise.
If you have a capable computer with decent RAM, you can also run AI models locally to use them for writing your email, summarising PDFs, data analysis, coding, using their vision capabilities, and much more.
However, setting up an AI model locally involves downloading the app, choosing the model yourself, and understanding its capabilities first.
To help you out, I have created this detailed, comprehensive guide to set up and run local AI models on your device on Android, iPhone, Mac, or even on Windows.
I wrote this guide with beginners in mind, so every step is comprehensive and easy to follow. If you have questions, comment below. I am happy to help you. Most of these models can run locally on many consumer applications, but before that, don’t forget to check our prerequisites because that’s where your journey starts.
Table of Contents
Pre-Requirements To Run AI Models Locally on Device
Your device’s RAM determines whether it can run AI models.
Technically, a model loads into your RAM to run. As a general rule of thumb, a model needs about as much free RAM as its download size.
So, more RAM leaves room to run large AI models. A minimum of 6 GB of RAM is required to run decent, capable AI models locally on your device
Similarly, you need enough storage to download and store models locally. A model can generally range from 2 GB to 20 GB or even more, depending on its size and capabilities.
Finally, you need an internet connection and enough data to download the model so you can run it offline.
As I said before, these models can range from 2 GB to 20 GB. So it requires an internet connection to download the model and store it locally on your device.
Of course, Other minimum specifications, such as a capable Processor, Operating system, and platform, also matter but not as much as RAM does.
How to check how much RAM your device has
On Android:
Go to About Device to see how much RAM your smartphone has. To do that: Open Settings on your device, tap on the search bar at the top, and search for “About Device”. On some phones, scroll down and tap “About Device”. Look at the RAM specifications.
On some phones, you will see extra visible RAM after the plus sign, for example, 16GB + 12GB. However, only the first number is the real memory.
iPhone:
Apple generally doesn’t disclose the RAM used in iPhones. However, iPhone 15 Pro and newer devices generally have at least 8GB, while older iPhones have less than 6GB, which can run 1 billion to 2 billion models. You can check how much RAM your iPhone has from here.
Mac:
To check how much RAM on your MacBook: From the home screen, click on the Apple icon in the top left corner screen and tap on About This Mac. From here, you can check chip and memory options. Apple MacBooks running on Apple Silicon are especially good for running local AI models since the graphics chip shares all the memory.
Windows:
On Windows, you can go to Settings > System > About. From there, check the installed RAM, graphics card, and system type (x86 or ARM-based), which determines which applications you can download to run AI models locally.
Once your device meets the minimum RAM requirement, follow these steps to set it up to run AI models locally. Use the table of contents above to go to the device you want to set up. This guide covers Android, iPhone, Mac, and Windows.
How to Run AI Models Locally on Any Device
Android:
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on Android with Google AI Edge Gallery
You can run Google’s family of Open-weight AI models locally for free on your Android device using Google’s own AI Edge Gallery app (Free).
Gemma 4 is Google’s latest open-weight model. It comes in five model sizes. Gemma 4 E2B and Gemma 4 E4B are suitable for running on Android devices. 2B requires at least 8GB of RAM, and 4B requires at least 12GB of RAM.
Gemma 4 also supports vision capabilities, so it is not just text; you can also use it to understand images.
How to install and run the latest Google Gemma 4 models locally on your Android phone
Step 1: Download Google AI Edge Gallery from the Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI Chat.
Step 3: Under the recommended models, tap Download below. To download the model you want. Gemma 4 E2B is 2.6 GB and best for starters, while Gemma 4 E4B is 3.7 GB and smarter, but your phone needs at least 8 GB of RAM to run it locally.
Step 3: Once the model is downloaded, tap Try it.
Step 4: Type your prompt in the Type prompt box and tap the send button.
Step 5: Like the other AI apps, the model replies to your prompt. You can also see how fast the model runs, measured in tokens per second, and how much RAM it uses. On my Android phone, the Gemma 4 E2B model ran at about 30 tokens per second, and my model comes with 16 GB of RAM.
Method 2: Run any open model on Android with PocketPal AI
PocketPal is a popular free and open-source app for running AI models locally on Android.
Unlike Google’s AI Edge Gallery, it supports a wide variety of third-party models, including Google’s Gemma, Meta’s Llama, Microsoft’s Phi, Qwen, and more. It also supports GGUF models, including compressed versions.
How do I use the PocketPal app to run AI models locally on my device?
Step 1: Download and install the PocketPal app from the Google Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and, during onboarding, tap Download Model.
Step 3: Pick any available model to download and tap Download,
or tap the plus option to find more. To get a new model, tap the plus icon, select Hugging Face, then tap Choose and add from Hugging Face.
Step 4: From here, you can search for any model. In this case, I searched for the Qwen3 1.7B parameter model and tapped the download icon to download it locally.
Step 5: Once done, open the Models tab and select the model to load it. Now go to the chat interface and enter the prompt, and the model uses the model that you have loaded, in this case, the Qwen3 1.7 billion parameter model, to answer your queries. You can also see how much time it takes to run this model on your device.
iPhone
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on iPhone with Google AI Edge Gallery
Google’s AI Edge Gallery is also available on iPhone and supports the latest Gemma 4 family of open-weight models, similar to Android. You can download and use E2B (around 2.6 GB) and the E4B model (around 3.7 GB).
Apple doesn’t disclose the RAM used on iPhones. However, the latest iPhone models, including the iPhone 15 Pro and later, support up to 8 GB of RAM, which can run these models faster and more reliably. However, older iPhones may struggle with slow responses, battery drain, and overheating, so keep that in mind.
Step 1: Download the Google AI Edge Gallery app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI chat
Step 3: Now download the compatible AI model. In this case, I’m downloading Gemma 4 E2B, which is about 2.59 GB. Click on the download icon under the model.
Step 4: Wait for the model to download, then tap Try It, enter the prompt, and wait for a reply. If you want to use the vision capabilities, tap on the plus icon and upload an image
Method 2: Run open models on iPhone with PocketPal AI
Similar to Google’s AI Edge Gallery app, the PocketPal app is also available on iPhone. It also gives access to some of the popular Hugging Face model library and other third-party models, including models from Meta, Cohere, and more. It also supports Google Gemma 4 models.
Step 1: Install the PocketPal AI app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app, tap Download Model, select a model, and tap Download. In this case, I am downloading the Qwen3 1.7B model.
Step 3: Once downloaded, tap the Load option at the top, enter the prompt, and wait for the reply
Mac
Method 1: Run AI models on a Mac with LM Studio
You can use LM Studio on Mac to run AI models locally.
It supports a wide range of models, including models from Google Gemma, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and more. Like the mobile app, you can install LM Studio on your Mac, download a model, and start chatting. It also supports GGUF and Apple-optimized MLX models.
Depending on the model, you can have text conversations, image analysis, and more. You can also use it as a local API for other apps.
However, LM Studio is only available on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later). Intel Macs are not supported.
How to install and run AI models locally using LM Studio on Mac
Step 1: First, go to lmstudio.ai/download and download the LM Studio app for Mac. Select the compatible version and drag and drop LM Studio into Applications to install it.
Step 2: Open LM Studio on the Mac, click on the model search in the sidebar, and search for the model; for example, in this case, I searched for the Gemma 4 E4B model
Step 3: You can also pick a different model, select it, and click Download. A likely fit badge here means that it is suitable to run locally on your Mac using your Mac’s available memory. Once the model is downloaded, tap on Use in the new chat instead.
Step 4: On the home screen, click Load Model in the dialog and select the model. You can also raise the context length here if you are planning for long conversations.
Step 5: Now enter the prompt and press Enter. The model returns with an option. You can also click the model server in the sidebar and turn on the status to use the model for other apps via an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:1234.
Method 2: Run AI models on a Mac with Ollama
You can also run AI models on your Mac using Ollama. It is a free, lightweight tool by Meta that lets you run local AI models in the terminal with one command. It also works with many local apps that support local AI.
Step 1: To run Ollama locally on your device, go to ollama.com/download and click on the Download manually option. You can also directly paste the command into the terminal if you are a developer.
Step 2: Next, open the Ollama.dmg, drag it into Applications, and open it
Step 3: On the onboarding screen, while setting up an account, Ollama asks you to sign up for an account; however, you can tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally’
Step 4: Next, to run ollama run llama3, copy the ollama run llama3 command, open Terminal, and paste it. Wait for the model to download completely. Ollama can run Qwen3 4B parameters and other models. In this case, I am going to run the Ollama run Qwen3 4B model. So, wait for the model to download completely.
Step 5: Finally, you can start using the Ollama model right there. You can enter the prompt directly, and it will reply in the same terminal.
Windows
Method 1: Run AI models on Windows with LM Studio
You can use the same LM Studio on Windows as well to run AI models locally on your device
Step 1: Download and install LM Studio for Windows. Here is the download page link.
Step 2: Open the LM Studio app and, in the left sidebar, tap Model Search and search for the model you want to run locally. In this case, Iam using Qwen3 1.7 billion parameters; on the model details page, click the download option.
Step 3: Wait for it to download, and once it has downloaded, tap on Use in new chat
Step 4: Now, on the home screen, in the model box, select the downloaded model. You can tap on the model to select and enable it, then enter the prompt and press enter.
Method 2: Run AI models on Windows with Ollama
Ollama is also available on Mac. It supports NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, as well as the latest ARM-based Snapdragon PCs. You can download models and use them directly from the terminal. Here is how.
Step 1: First, download Ollama on Windows. Go to ollama.com/download/windows and click Manual download. If you are a developer, you can install it directly in PowerShell using the PowerShell command.
Step 2: Now install the Ollama app on Windows. While setting up, click Continue, and then tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally, so you can skip creating an account.
Step 3: Next, copy the command shown in the app, open Terminal, and run this command: ollama run qwen3:1.7b, and press Enter. It downloads the model. Wait for the download to complete.
Step 4: Now enter your question and press Enter.
This is how you can set up and run AI models locally on Android, iPhone, Windows, and Mac. Choosing the right model is important to get high-quality output. Bigger models don’t always mean better outputs, as their capabilities can vary. Our guide to the best AI models to run locally should help you choose the right model for your needs.
