Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MLA Paresh Ram Das was arrested on Monday (November 9, 2026) from Kolkata’s Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Police said there were several charges against the Canning Paschim MLA including extortion and rape.
According to police sources, the Special Operations Group (SOG) of Baruipur district police began tracking the MLA after receiving information that he was heading to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Mr. Das had defeated his nearest rival, BJP candidate from Canning Paschim by a margin of over 40,000 votes.
The team subsequently contacted the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate, following which the MLA was arrested. Mr. Das is among the handful of MLAs that have remained with former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.
Mamata AITC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said that as he was with the rebel camp, the police were inactive but when the MLA pledged his alliance to Ms. Banerjee, he was arrested. Recently, the MLA has put a post of social media, stating “Alvida Canning. We will meet again”.
Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers, including Bishnupur MLA Dilip Mondal. The list of former Ministers who are behind bars includes Sujit Bose, Indranil Sen, Ujjwal Biswas and Udayan Guha.
The Mamata Banerjee loyalists claim that leaders, MLAs and former Ministers who have joined the rebel camp led by Ritabrata Banerjee are being given a reprieve by the police while those still having allegiance to the former Chief Minister are being arrested.

అమెరికాలోని న్యూయార్క్ ఎయిర్పోర్ట్లో ఇమ్మిగ్రేషన్ అధికారులకు ఒక మహిళ పట్టుబడిందని, ఆమె తన దేశం పేరు “టొరెంజో” అని చెప్పిందని, అసలు ఉనికిలో లేని ఈ దేశం పేరుతోనే ఆమె పాస్పోర్ట్ కూడా కలిగి ఉందని పేర్కొంటూ ఒక వీడియో సోషల్ మీడియాలో ప్రచారమవుతోంది. దీంట్లో ఎంత నిజముందో ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: న్యూయార్క్ ఎయిర్పోర్ట్లో ప్రపంచంలో ఉనికిలోనే లేని “టొరెంజో” అనే దేశం నుండి వచ్చిన ఒక ప్రయాణికురాలిని చూపుతున్న వీడియో.
ఫాక్ట్: ఈ ప్రచారం పూర్తిగా కల్పితం, అసలు ఇలాంటి ఘటన జరిగినట్లు ఆధారాలు లేవు. వైరల్ వీడియో వాస్తవానికి 2004లో ప్రసారమైన ‘ఎయిర్లైన్’ అనే అమెరికన్ రియాలిటీ టీవీ సిరీస్లోని ఒక దృశ్యం. ఫుటేజ్లో లాస్ ఏంజెలెస్కు ప్రయాణించిన ఒక అరబిక్ మాట్లాడే వృద్ధురాలిని చూపించారు తప్ప, “టొరెంజో” అనే ప్రస్తావన ఎక్కడా లేదు. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పు.
ముందుగా, ఈ విషయం గురించి ఇంటర్నెట్లో వెతకగా, ఇటువంటి ఘటన జరిగినట్లు ఎటువంటి విశ్వసనీయ వార్తా కథనాలు లభించలేదు. ఇక వైరల్ వీడియోలోని దృశ్యాలను రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, దీనికి సంబంధించిన పూర్తి వీడియోను (ఆర్కైవ్ 1, ఆర్కైవ్ 2) A&E యూట్యూబ్ ఛానెల్లో 08 నవంబర్ 2024న “Airline: Best Full Episodes of 2024 MARATHON | A&E” అనే శీర్షికతో అప్లోడ్ చేసినట్లు గుర్తించాము.ప్రస్తుతం ఈ వీడియో ప్రైవేట్ చేయబడింది.
దీని గురించి మరింత పరిశోధించగా, ఈ వైరల్ వీడియో వాస్తవానికి 2004-2005 మధ్య A&Eలో ప్రసారమైన ‘ఎయిర్లైన్’ అనే అమెరికన్ రియాలిటీ టీవీ సిరీస్లోని ఒక దృశ్యమని తేలింది. ఇది ప్రయాణికులతో సౌత్వెస్ట్ ఎయిర్లైన్స్ సిబ్బంది జరిపే రోజువారీ సంభాషణలను చూపుతుంది. వైరల్ వీడియోలో ఉన్న దృశ్యాలు, ఈ యూట్యూబ్ వీడియోలోని మొదటి ఎపిసోడ్లో 22వ నిమిషం వద్ద ప్రారంభమవుతాయి. ఈ దృశ్యాలు బాల్టిమోర్ నుండి లాస్ ఏంజెలెస్కు ప్రయాణించిన, ఆంగ్లం రాని ఒక వృద్ధురాలిని చూపుతాయి.
ఈ వీడియోలో, ఆమె పాస్పోర్ట్ ఇంగ్లీషులో లేదని గమనించిన ఒక ఎయిర్లైన్ ఉద్యోగి, “సౌదీ అరేబియా, వాళ్ళు అరబిక్ మాట్లాడతారు కదా?” అని చెబుతూ ఆమెను అరబిక్ మాట్లాడే వ్యక్తిగా గుర్తిస్తారు. ఇందులో ఎక్కడా కూడా “టొరెంజో” అనే ప్రదేశం ప్రస్తావనే లేదు. ఆ తర్వాత సిబ్బంది ఆమెను అరబిక్ మాట్లాడే మరో ఉద్యోగితో మాట్లాడిస్తారు, చివరకు ఆమెను తీసుకెళ్లడానికి ఆమె మేనల్లుడు ఎయిర్పోర్ట్కు వస్తారు.
దీన్ని బట్టి, వైరల్ వీడియోలో చెప్పిన విషయాలు నిజం కాదని, వాస్తవానికి ఆ ఫుటేజ్ ఒక టెలివిజన్ సిరీస్కు చెందినదని నిర్ధారించవచ్చు.
చివరిగా, ఉనికిలో లేని “టొరెంజో” దేశం నుండి ఒక మహిళ వచ్చిందంటూ, ఒక అమెరికన్ టెలివిజన్ సిరీస్కు చెందిన దృశ్యాలను తప్పుగా ప్రచారం చేస్తున్నారు.

- The Differential Microphones can be found only in the Pendola Pass map.

Arc Raiders Frozen Trail update introduced many new crafting items that let players build outposts, amplify weapons, and more. One of the most sought-after items is the Differential Microphone, which is vital to upgrading the new Research Station in the game. So, here is how to get the Differential Microphone in Arc Raiders.
How to Get the Differential Microphone in Arc Raiders
The Differential Microphone is a completely new rare-type crafting resource material added in the Arc Raiders Frozen Trail update. Thus, the Differential Microphones spawn only in the all-new Pendola Pass map in Arc Raiders.
Fortunately, you don’t have to defeat any ARC enemy in Arc Raiders to get a Differential Microphone. Instead, you can find it in open spaces as well as inside various containers in the game.
Differential Microphone Spawn Locations in Arc Raiders
As mentioned earlier, Differential Microphones spawn only in the Pendola Pass map in Arc Raiders, especially in the Technological and Electrical sections. So, here are the best loot zones you need to head to if you want to get a Differential Microphone in Arc Raiders:
- Almatera Station
- Cielo Sereno Observatory
- Commissary Supermarket
- Freight Terminal
As Pendola Pass features dynamic loot zones, the high-value loot items keep shifting. But you can find a Differential Microphone in our recommended spots on the map. So, keep checking the containers, cupboards, shelves, tables, chairs, vehicles, etc., and you can soon collect the three Differential Microphones you need for upgrades.
Differential Microphone Uses in Arc Raiders
Currently, Differential Microphones are used to upgrade the Research Station to level 3 once you establish an Outpost in Arc Raiders. You need 3 Differential Microphones along with Bully Fragmenter and Exodus Technical Handbook to upgrade to Research Station Level 3.
| Resource Material | Crafting | Upgrade | Recycling | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Differential Microphone | 3× Differential Microphone 3× Exodus Technical Handbook 6× Bully Fragmenter | Unlock Research Station Level 3 | 1× Speaker Component 2× Wires | 
In addition, you can also recycle a Differential Microphone to get a Speaker Component and Wires for crafting other items in the game.

The GTA series has fundamentally always been about stealing cars, robbing stores, escaping the cops, and killing people with minimal consequences. You rob another car, the cops catch you, and you do it all over again without a care in the world.
No sleep, no food, just endless chaos in an open-world sandbox. However, the more I learn about GTA 6’s in-depth mechanics, the more I feel like Rockstar is trying to make me live inside the game with its life-sim elements, rather than play it.
With new systems like maintaining Jason and Lucia’s relationship, tracking their calorie intake and weight, registering vehicles under your name, and even depositing money in the bank, Rockstar seems to be going all-in on immersion.
But this obsession with making GTA 6 feel hyperrealistic and immersive could end up taking away what makes the series so much fun in the first place, and here’s why.
I Want to Play as Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, Not Manage Them
In my opinion, there’s a clear conflict between immersion and fun in GTA 6. For the first time, I feel like I’ll have to consciously take care of both Jason and Lucia instead of playing GTA 6 however I want, as I did in previous GTA games. I had similar issues in Red Dead Redemption 2’s life-sim elements, but they were negligible since it’s a Red Dead title.
For a GTA title, this is completely new. Now, I have to maintain Jason and Lucia’s relationship by doing different activities in GTA 6 together, texting each other, working out to keep their stats and attributes in check, and even getting enough sleep to avoid exhaustion.
There’s a lot more to these life-sim and roleplay elements in GTA 6. While these details make the characters feel more alive, it also starts to feel like I’m managing their lives rather than playing as them. I always did take care of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in GTA 5, but it didn’t feel like something you had to do.
In GTA 6, I feel like the moment I open my save file, I have to wonder what I’ve neglected. Did Jason and Lucia sleep well? Are they well fed? Have I spent enough time with each other? Are they angry at one another? What can I do to fix it?
Sure, it’s immersive, extremely, if I’m being honest, but is it convenient? I do want the best for the characters I play with, as long as it’s fun and doesn’t feel forced.
GTA 6’s Immersion Is Starting to Feel Like a Second Life
With Jason and Lucia out of the way, let’s discuss some features I personally think shouldn’t be in a GTA game. For example, GTA 6’s refueling mechanic. I never stopped to think about how much fuel I have left in a GTA game when running from the cops, chasing an NPC, or in any other situation.
It feels more like an evolution of the horse’s stamina mechanic from Red Dead Redemption 2 than a genuinely meaningful addition. Is it immersive? Absolutely. But I can also see it getting repetitive pretty quickly. Next up in the coterie of life-sim roleplay elements is how GTA 6’s cash acts like the real thing.
You now have to deposit your cash, earn specific amounts of money to progress certain GTA 6 missions, and even worry about other robbers stealing the money you’re carrying. When it comes to stealing cars, there’s a tiered security system and specialized tools to steal one, as the Slim Jim showcased in the GTA 6 Extended Look.
So, you can no longer steal exotic rides the moment you start your GTA 6 playthrough. You’ll need to earn your way up to it, and later register it under your name if you want to own it. This is where GTA 6’s fully functional public transport system chimes in. As I said, it’s all extremely immersive.
You can even doomscroll with your in-game phone and the apps in GTA 6, making it feel more like living a second life than simply playing a game.
Rockstar is clearly building on the foundations they’ve set with Red Dead Redemption 2, and that’s what worries me. It’s all incredibly immersive, but I can’t help feeling these life-sim systems could come at the cost of the classic GTA fun we’ve always loved.
GTA 6 Is Replacing the Series’ Power Fantasy with Real Consequences
In previous GTA outings like San Andreas, Vice City, or even 5, you were borderline overpowered. Play how you want, shoot whoever you want, launch a missile straight into the Los Santos Police Department, and you could still come out of the entire fiasco alive, without losing anything (except maybe your life if you mess up).
On the other hand, GTA 6’s Criminal Profile brings in new consequences for Jason and Lucia’s actions. It’s another life-sim element I’m worried about. For those unaware, the Criminal Profile will limit how you approach and play certain situations, and in most cases, killing everyone will be a no-no.
The cleaner you pull off your crimes, the better your Criminal Profile gets. But you can also permanently shatter it if you reach the “Irredeemable” state, and honestly, I’d hate to mess up my entire playthrough for a little fun and possibly end up with a worse ending.
Additionally, the cops in GTA 6 are far smarter than in previous entries. They can remember your clothes, your appearance, your vehicle, and even whether you were with Jason or Lucia when the crime happened.
These life-sim and roleplay elements in GTA 6 may hinder the series’ power fantasy, with Rockstar taking a more believable and consequential approach. It’s for immersion, I know, and players can tailor their experience to their own liking, but how immersive is too immersive?
Because it looks like I’ll need a separate manual save to have the traditional GTA fun, because Jason and Lucia will have too much to lose in my main GTA 6 playthrough. To me, it feels like Rockstar was so preoccupied with adding these life-sim elements to GTA 6 that they didn’t stop to think about whether they should.
However, despite it all, I have secured my GTA 6 pre-order and am very much looking forward to testing these roleplaying systems myself. I’d love to be wrong, and I genuinely hope these realistic life-sim mechanics enhance the overall experience without taking away from the chaotic, unpredictable GTA gameplay that made me fall in love with the series in the first place.

An unidentified person allegedly sexually assaulted a three-year-old girl at a dilapidated building in North Goa district, police said on Monday.

After Michigan voters elected Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as senator in November 2026, a claim (archived) circulated online that he had failed the background check required for classified Senate briefings.
One X user named Jonathan Gregory who shared the claim wrote that El-Sayed's alleged failure would exclude him from some meetings as a senator. The user wrote:
Abdul El Sayed has failed the background check required for classified Senate briefings. The denial blocks him from any session that involves sensitive national security information. Officials who conduct the clearances reported that the review did not meet the standards necessary for access to restricted materials. The failure leaves open the question of what specific issues prevented approval.
Senators who receive classified briefings must clear the same process before they can attend. El Sayed's rejection means he cannot participate in those meetings. The decision places him outside the normal flow of information that other members receive. Americans who expect every senator to qualify for the same briefings now see one individual excluded by the clearance system.
(@TrumpNews_Baby, accessed via X)
The claim also circulated on Facebook (archived). Snopes readers contacted us to verify whether it was true.
The claim was false. El-Sayed could not have "failed" a background check "required for classified Senate briefings" because no such background check exists.
Congress members, including senators, are not required to pass a background check to gain security clearance and access classified material, according to a Congressional Research Service "Frequently Asked Questions" report about security clearances from 2023.
The U.S. Constitution, which lays out the requirements for senators, does not include a requirement for them to pass a background check to access classified information. According to Constitution Annotated, the Library of Congress' legal analysis and interpretation of the Constitution, the document has never allowed for changes to the requirements for a senator because that would undermine the legislative branch's investigative powers.
Additionally, federal law exempts members of Congress, including senators, from legislation that governs background checks and security clearances.
The false rumor may have originated as satire. Snopes previously linked another false claim about election fraud to Jonathan Gregory, who shared the first instance of the rumor about El-Sayed that we identified on X. Gregory labels himself as a comedian on his Facebook page, though his Instagram and X accounts don't display such a label. None of Gregory's profiles specifically mention the word "satire," though he has previously used the term near the very end of some of his posts — potentially as a way of hinting at the truth about his content.
We've published fact checks about other matters originating from Gregory's social media accounts, all of which involved false claims.
We contacted El-Sayed's campaign to ask if he had ever applied for, been granted or denied government security clearance before becoming a senator-elect. We also asked the national intelligence director's office whether it had ever granted or denied security clearance to El-Sayed in the past. We await replies to our questions.
Congress investigative powers allow members access to classified information
Members of Congress are implicitly allowed to access classified information because the U.S. Constitution gives the legislative branch investigative powers to inform laws and ensure they are being carried out. In practice, carrying out these investigations can mean that members of Congress need to access classified material, and the Information Security Oversight Office, which is responsible for the policy and oversight of the U.S. government's security classification system, wrote in 2001 that this is generally allowed (PDF Page 66).
It is important to note, however, that though El-Sayed and any other member of Congress bypass the normal procedure for getting security clearance, that does not give them unlimited access to classified information.
For example, the ISOO wrote in 2001 that though members of Congress were exempt from background checks and filling out the government's classified information nondisclosure agreement, they were not exempt from the "'need-to-know' requirement" (PDF Page 66).
For example, the office wrote (PDF Page 66) that members of Congress, "are not inherently authorized to receive all classified information, but agencies provide access as is necessary for Congress to perform its legislative functions."
Subject to election certification by state officials, the 120th Congress, which will include El-Sayed as one of two senators from Michigan, will be sworn in on Jan. 3, 2027.
For further reading, Snopes frequently investigates rumors relating to El-Sayed.

A promising new medicine against heart disease fails unexpectedly
For stories on the science of healthy living, subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
An experimental drug doctors hoped would be the next big advance in preventing heart attacks and strokes failed a crucial test, researchers reported Saturday.
The medicine, which reduces levels of a particle in the blood associated with heart attacks and strokes, didn't protect volunteers in a closely watched study.
"I was shocked. I had high hopes for success," says Steven Nissen, a cardiologist at the Cleveland Clinic who led the study. "Cardiovascular disease is still the leading cause of death in developed countries. And so we really were hoping to find additional therapies that would reduce risk."
The research aimed to help people who seem to do everything right. They keep their cholesterol and blood pressure low, eat well, maintain a healthy weight, and exercise regularly. But many still suffer heart attacks and strokes.
"That sort of patient we see very frequently, and we were really doing our best to try to find a way to help those patients," Nissen says.
Many of these patients have elevated blood levels of a cholesterol-carrying protein called lipoprotein(a) or Lp(a), which has long been thought to increase the risk for heart disease.
"About 20% of the global population have elevated levels. And that's about a billion people. So it's a common disorder," Nissen says.
Researchers have been searching for a drug to lower Lp(a)
Until recently, doctors didn't have any drugs that could lower Lp(a) levels. But several drug companies have developed experimental new medications in recent years that can slash elevated Lp(a).
So Nissen and his colleagues gave 8,350 adults who already had heart disease either a placebo or a drug called pelacarsen, which cuts Lp(a).
The drug did suppress Lp(a) levels by about 78%, the researchers showed. But after five years, that drop didn't translate into saving people from suffering cardiovascular complications.
"Very disappointing, terribly disappointing," says Nissen, who presented the first details about the study at an American Heart Association meeting in Chicago Saturday and published more specifics in the New England Journal of Medicine and the NEJM Evidence.
Drugmaker Novartis, which sponsored the study, announced last month that the study results hadn't met its goals but without releasing specifics.
In a statement, Novartis said the study "provides meaningful evidence" about the relationship between Lp(a) and heart disease and may "help inform future approaches to cardiovascular management." "Progress in science depends on pursuing challenging questions and studies [like the pelacarsen study] play a crucial role in moving the field forward, even if the results are not what we had hoped for," the company said.
What went wrong?
The failure of the drug to help patients is stunning because so many scientists, doctors and drug companies hoped Lp(a)-lowering drugs would provide the next major weapon in the fight against cardiovascular disease, which kills more than 900,000 Americans each year.
"I think it's a big deal because the expectation was so high that this would end up being positive," says Harlan Krumholz, a Yale University cardiologist. "And so it was really jarring to see this."
Researchers are scratching their heads about what went wrong.
It could turn out that high Lp(a) doesn't actually cause heart attacks and strokes, but instead is a marker for something else that increases the risk.
There could be other reasons for why the study failed.
"Maybe you need to treat longer. You may need to treat earlier, before people have advanced hardening of the arteries," says Roger Blumenthal, a cardiologist at Johns Hopkins University.
Another possibility is that Lp(a)-lowering drugs may only help people with higher Lp(a) levels.
"Maybe a higher Lp(a) should have been required for entry into the trial," says David Maron, a Stanford University cardiologist who serves as the president of the American Society for Preventive Cardiology.
The pelacarsen study could also have failed because Lp(a)-lowering drugs may only benefit people whose blood pressure and bad cholesterol weren't as well controlled, several experts said.
Another explanation could be that there's something about pelacarsen, the experimental drug, that doesn't produce a benefit.
It's possible other Lp(a)-lowering drugs might.
Several other drugmakers, including Amgen and Eli Lilly, are testing other experimental Lp(a)-lowering drugs. The results of those trials are expected to become available over the next few years.
"The take-home message is the story's not over," says Karol Watson, a cardiologist at the University of California, Los Angeles. "It's kind of just starting."

Three family members, including 20-day-old baby, killed as house roof collapses in Kanpur
The incident took place in Panki Padav area when the roof, made of bamboo, wooden beams and mud, suddenly gave way.
Three members of a family, including a 20-day-old baby, were killed in Uttar Pradesh' Kanpur when the roof of a room in their house collapsed on Sunday morning.
The deceased have been identified as Vinodini Shukla, 60, her daughter-in-law Anshika 28, and 20-day-old grandson. Harsh Shukla 32, who was also present inside the room when the roof caved in, sustained minor injuries.
The incident took place in Panki Padav area when the roof, made of bamboo, wooden beams and mud, suddenly gave way. Family members and neighbours rushed to remove the debris and pulled out the occupants who were then taken to Kalyanpur Community Health Centre. Doctors declared the three dead.
According to a relative Manoj Bajpai, the family were busy with their morning chores on Diwali, while Harsh and his mother were sitting in the room. Anshika was feeding their newborn and other members of the family, including Harsh's father Avadhesh Shukla, 65, and younger brother Raju, 29, were in another room when the roof collapsed.
The house, owned by Avadhesh, is around 35 years old. The single-storey house has four rooms, with a roof constructed using bamboo, wooden beams and mud.
DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said police had received information about three deaths following the roof collapse. “Prima facie, it appears that water seepage increased the load on the roof,” he said.
The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. A revenue team was also present at the spot, and further legal proceedings were underway.

Book Box: Diwali and the books we give each other
A reflection on parent-child bonds, nostalgic reading, and recommended books for the festive season.
Dear Reader,
It is Diwali morning in Mumbai. Four days ago we left the new home we are still making. The carpenters caught a bus home to Mandi, the masons to Bajaura, the polisher to Bilaspur. The Other Reader and I drove down to the plains, to Chandigarh, and flew to Mumbai to spend Diwali with my parents and my siblings.
In Mumbai, my mother needs containers for her kitchen. Little jars for cardamom, cinnamon, cumin. We go together to the neighbourhood market. The shop down the road is crammed with containers of every kind. My mother finds what she wants. Flushed with the hunter-gatherer thrill of a successful expedition, we go for cold coffee at Poetry and Cheesecake. We share a frappe and talk about how to parent adult children.
The waitress, a friendly young woman in her twenties, brings us the bill inside an anthology of poetry.
My mother pays. Then she opens the book. “’There was a ship,” quoth he,” she begins, and we are both gone. Back to a bungalow in Jamshedpur. Back to the evenings when she read to us, sometimes The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, sometimes The Highwayman.
“It’s been so long,” she says, “since I read aloud.”
She asks if she can buy the book. The waitress smiles and says no. They don’t sell these. It is the only copy, kept for bringing bills to customers. Then she looks at our faces and says, “You can borrow it.”
I want to tell her how much this means to me. My mother has been a little sad and overwhelmed of late, and these poems are just what she needs. I want her to know that this small gesture has made my mother very happy.
Instead, I say, “Thank you, thank you. I live just down the road. I’ll leave my number.”
“That’s okay,” she says. “Just drop it back.”
In the car my mother worries. “I hope she doesn’t get into trouble.” But she is already turning pages, finding her favourites one by one. “Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?” she reads.
“These are the poems I really love. And this print is large enough for my eyes,” she says.
Tonight, after the diyas, we will read them aloud. Tomorrow morning I will take the book back. I hope the young woman is there. I want to tell her what it meant to my mother.
Yesterday the book club met, and it was different. We came dressed in saris. We swapped books, which seemed apt for Diwali. We laughed and joked and squabbled a little. Everyone wanted Leftovers:A History of Food Waste and Preservation by Dr. Eleanor Barnett. Everyone wanted Prayers for Rain, a murder mystery by Dennis Lehane. Nobody wanted Swallowing the Sun by Lakshmi Murdeshwar Puri, a striking hardback with a beautiful cover and a slow-moving story inside.
If you are still looking for books to give this Diwali, here are a few possibilities.
· The one everyone’s talking about: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke, a satirical suspense novel about a tradwife influencer.
· Feel-good novels about human relationships : Whistler by Ann Patchett or The Correspondent by Virginia Evans.
· Poetry for the shelf: Glass, Irony and God by this year’s Nobel laureate Anne Carson, which includes the extraordinary The Glass Essay. And perhaps an anthology of the fifty greatest poets : something to dip into, and something to read aloud.
· Non-fiction: London Falling by Patrick Radden Keefe, a true story about a London teenager’s death set against an extraordinary landscape of crime in the city. Or Marginlands by Arati Kumar-Rao, a book that explores India’s vulnerable landscapes and the people who live in them.
Our borrowed poetry anthology is on the table by the door, to be read aloud and then given back.
Happy Diwali and happy reading. I’d love to know: is there a poem someone read to you as a child that you still remember?
Sonya Dutta Choudhury is a Mumbai-based journalist, Founder of Sonya’s Book Box, and a teacher of Storytelling in Business. Got a knot in your life, a dilemma at work, or a reading slump you can’t shake? Send your questions and book requests to sonyasbookbox@gmail.com, and she promises to give each one her most earnest consideration.

‘Diwali is Diwali, Eid is Eid’: BJP slams Mallikarjun Kharge over festival remark
The row stems from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s choice of words when he extended his Diwali greetings to people on Saturday
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday launched a sharp attack on the Congress leadership, accusing party president Mallikarjun Kharge of appeasement politics and of hurting Hindu sentiments by calling Diwali the “Eid of happiness”.
The row stems from Kharge’s remarks when he extended his Diwali greetings to people on Saturday, saying this is a major festival celebrated by everyone across the country as it is a “khushiyon ka Eid” that lasts for a long time.
“Diwali is Diwali, and Eid is Eid. Why is it that when it comes to Diwali which has its own sanctity, tradition and identity, you choose to call it Eid while extending greetings to Hindus?” said BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia on Monday, alleging that the Congress sought to dilute the identity of Hindu festivals.
Union minister Giriraj Singh said this wasn’t a one-off remark and linked Kharge’s remarks to the Congress leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and his family.
Congress leader Pawan Khera said Eid was often used as a metaphor for joy.
Hitting back at the BJP, Khera said, “Does anybody in the BJP have a dictionary in their house? I am sure they don’t. But they have a mobile. Can they Google what Eid means? Eid means ‘tyohar’, Diwali ka ‘tyohar’, Holi ka ‘tyohar’ - that’s what he means.”
Congress leader Rashid Alvi made the same point. “Clearly, when it comes to expressing joy, Eid is often used as a metaphor, much like how, when someone reappears after a long absence, people ask, ‘Kya tum Eid ka chand ho gaye ho?’ Eid is synonymous with joy,” he said.
Bhatia said Kharge’s choice of words reflected the Congress leadership’s broader approach towards Hindu religious traditions. “This is the DNA of the Congress party. First, indulging in blatant appeasement of the Muslim community and second, hurting the sentiments of the Hindu community,” he said.
The BJP spokesperson also took issue with Alvi’s reference to air quality, alleging that Congress leaders selectively raised pollution concerns around Diwali while failing to speak about other forms of pollution. “Discrimination and selective outrage are precisely what these people indulge in,” Bhatia added.
Accusing the Congress of following a selective definition of secularism, Bhatia said, “The Congress party’s definition of secularism is to silence the majority. You have to silence the majority and surrender to the radicals.”

A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.
Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5), indicating a “moderate” brain injury, just one point above “mild.” He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5).
In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head.
“Pull-and-see”
The blade was entirely through the right eye socket and eyeball. It traversed the left frontal and temporal lobes of his brain, passing through in front of—and without apparently injuring—the corpus callosum, which connects the two sides of the brain and is full of nerve fibers. The blade also missed the left internal capsule, which holds another bundle of nerve fibers.
In terms of damage to major blood vessels, doctors found that the blade was close to the left internal carotid artery, a major blood vessel, but didn’t seem to have damaged it. Doctors did find, however, that a branch of the middle cerebral artery looked to be indented by the knife.
After consulting with various medical specialties, the man’s doctors moved to emergency neurosurgery. They opted to remove part of his skull to directly see into the brain, but used a conservative “pull-and-see” method to slide the blade out rather than invasively excavate it. After it was out, the doctors saw no signs of significant hemorrhaging. The brain wound was cleaned and drained before surgeons patched up his skull. His right eye, however, couldn’t be saved. Given its extensive damage, it was removed.

Tesla will end production of the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory next year.
It’s a uniquely toxic electric vehicle, between its divisive design and Elon Musk’s embrace of you name it. That toxicity certainly contributed to subpar sales, along with a number of recalls.
But the end of the Cybertruck is also another sign that the era of big EVs—particularly big trucks—is waning. That’s great news for pedestrian and biker safety, but also for the battery supply chain at a time when more people need to get behind the electric wheel.
The Cybertruck uses a massive 123 kilowatt-hour battery that clocks in at around 1,600 pounds, or around a quarter of its weight. That’s on par with the battery that powered Ford’s F-150 Lightning, another electric truck that was canceled late last year. (The company also killed a three-row EV in 2024.) Ford’s behemoth batteries ranged from 98 kilowatt-hours up to 131 kilowatt-hours.
Seeing both trucks canceled within a year of each other, while automakers have announced a bevy of smaller EVs and gas-powered autos with electric motors that can extend range, indicates there may be a shift afoot. Ford is planning to launch the Fathom next year. The sub-$30,000 electric pickup is expected to be about the size of the automaker’s compact gas-powered Maverick pickup. Though Ford hasn’t announced the battery sizes available in various trims, it’s a safe bet they won’t be anywhere near the size of the F-150 Lightning or Cybertruck. The company is also planning to relaunch the Lightning as an extended-range model.
Startup Slate is also launching a tiny electric pickup that can be converted to an SUV, with a bare-bones base model starting below $25,000. It also features a svelte battery and has seen a massive surge in preorders—though, to be fair, so did the Cybertruck, and we saw that turned out.
Then there’s the Rivian R2, which launched this year. While the SUV isn’t as tiny or cheap as Ford and Slate’s vehicles—its battery has 88 kilowatt-hours of capacity and weighs in at around 1,200 pounds—it’s still smaller than the company’s flagship R1S. Rivian has also teased the R3, an even more-slimmed down SUV, in the coming years.
That’s not to say big EVs are dead. The Kia EV9, for example, is among the top 10 EVs by sales in the US, as is the R1S. There’s also a torrid resale market for the F-150 Lightning. But the rest of the top 10 new EV sales are all crossovers, sedans, or mid-sized SUVs with moderately sized batteries, and a number of newly announced EVs are trending on the smaller side or function as extended range vehicles.
Building smaller vehicles is, of course, one way to make EVs cheaper. With less weight to propel, you can rely on a smaller battery. And given that the battery pack is the most costly component of an EV, that can in turn help automakers offer more affordable vehicles at a time when the price of so many other consumer goods is skyrocketing. That includes the current crop of EVs: The average transaction price for a new model is now $55,800, according to Cox Automotive.
Going small—or smaller, anyway—also means making the most of a limited battery supply chain. The vast majority of Cybertruck drivers are doing the same thing with their vehicles as Hyundai Ioniq 5 drivers: getting groceries, commuting, and driving kids to soccer games. But a standard range Ioniq 5 driver is doing it with a battery about half the size.
After President Donald Trump’s administration killed EV incentives last year, sales plummeted. The Iran War and rising gas prices have led to an uptick in interest, though sales still lag behind the global average. (Used hybrid sales have also picked up, reflecting the pain people have been feeling at the pump.) Even with a Democratic-controlled Congress, EV incentives coming back under Trump are about as likely as defense secretary Pete Hegseth putting pronouns in his email signature. But should Democrats take the White House in 2028, marking the culmination of Woke 2.0, support for would-be EV buyers becomes much more likely.
Automakers pivoting to smaller cars could be much better-positioned to meet pent-up demand if that happens, while also lowering the risks of delivery delays.
Even Elon’s announcement killing the Cybertruck points to where the market is heading: He claims Tesla is ending production to make room for cranking out more Cybercabs. The battery size in those vehicles? Just 48 kilowatt-hours.

New Delhi, Nov 9: Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.
As of Monday morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.
The government's decision not to prorogue (formally end) the Monsoon session has kept alive speculation about the possibility of convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional amendment linked to the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.
An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.
This has added significance as a similar Constitution Amendment Bill had failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget session on April 17.
The Constitution does not prescribe any specific time frame within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period).
The mere fact that a House remains unprorogued for an extended period does not, by itself, amount to any constitutional or procedural impropriety.
According to records, Parliament had remained unprorogued for 87 days in 2008, 76 days in 1987, 54 days in 1989, 49 days each in 2006 and 2013, and 41 days in 1963.
In 2008, the Lok Sabha met for two days, July 21 and 22, to discuss the no-confidence motion against the then UPA government. The House was subsequently kept unprorogued, reconvened on October 17 and was adjourned on October 24 to meet again on December 10.

One killed in Indonesia helicopter crash during firefighting operation
- Published
One person has died after a helicopter crashed into a river in Indonesia during a mission to fight wildfires in South Kalimantan.
An Indonesian crew member was killed, while two others on board - an Australian and New Zealander - were "found safe" and taken to hospital for treatment, according to Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency.
Investigations into the accident are ongoing, the agency said on Sunday, adding that it could continue its firefighting operations.
For months, parts of Indonesia have been battling wildfires that have shrouded large swathes of South East Asia in toxic haze. The blazes in forests and peatlands are fuelled by a dry season that has been exacerbated by El Niño.
Videos posted by Indonesia's disaster authorities and circulating on social media show the helicopter hovering over the river with a helicopter bucket - a collapsible container typically used to douse water over fires - before it nosedives into the water.
Other videos show rescuers later reaching the partially submerged helicopter by boat.
The fallen chopper, a Super Puma H-225, was owned by a company that disaster authorities had contracted for the firefighting operations, a disaster official told AFP.
The incident comes days after another helicopter crashed in central Kalimantan during a firefighting operation, killing three crew members.
The military said on Saturday that they had managed to retrieve the helicopter's blackbox, which would help their investigations into the cause of the crash.
Despite intensive firefighting efforts, the wildfires in Indonesia this year have been especially difficult to tame due to drought conditions exacerbated by a stronger El Niño.
The raging wildfires sent toxic smog blanketing cities in Indonesia, turning the air amber and triggering a surge in respiratory illnesses in cities across the islands of Kalimantan and Sumatra.
The haze also drifted to neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore, where it has triggered public health concerns.
Foreign governments have sent assistance to help with firefighting efforts, including Australia, which has deployed aircraft and 20 personnel including pilots and paramedics.

The Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to immediately suspend the manufacturing licences of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified critical quality parameters.
The government said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards, in the interest of patient safety and public health.
Under the existing provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. This may result in a time gap between the declaration of a drug as NSQ and the initiation of regulatory action. During this period, the drug may remain in circulation, posing potential risks to public health and making effective recall more challenging.
To address this regulatory concern, the Ministry has proposed a provision for immediate suspension of the manufacturing licence of the drug by the Central Licensing Approving Authority or the State Licensing Authority upon receipt of a government analyst’s report declaring the drug as NSQ with respect to assay, dissolution, related substances, impurities or sterility.
“These parameters are critical to determining the quality of medicines. The proposed provision aims to ensure that instances of non-compliance involving these specified parameters are met with prompt regulatory action, thereby minimising potential risks to patients,’’ the Ministry said.
The proposed amendment provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective root cause analysis to identify the reasons for the quality failure and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the licensing authority.
Suspension can be revoked after the requisite corrective and preventive measures are implemented and then verified by the licensing authority. This mechanism will ensure that identified quality deficiencies are adequately addressed and necessary safeguards are put in place to prevent their recurrence.
“To further strengthen regulatory coordination and facilitate timely action, consequential amendments have also been proposed to Form 13, relating to the test report of the Government Analyst. Under the proposed mechanism, the Government Analyst’s report would be endorsed to the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), the concerned State/UT Licensing Authority under whose jurisdiction the manufacturing site is located, as well as the manufacturer and marketer of the concerned drug,’’ the government said.
It added that the proposed arrangement is aimed at ensuring timely communication of NSQ findings to the relevant authorities and stakeholders, thereby facilitating coordinated regulatory action and strengthening accountability across the drug manufacturing and marketing chain.
The proposed amendments follow deliberations at the 65th meeting of the Drugs Consultative Committee, held on December 20, 2024, and recommendations of the 92nd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board, held on April 24, 2025.
The amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers, and reinforce public confidence in the quality of medicines available in the country.
The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation, inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette of India containing the draft rules are made available to the public.

(Bloomberg) -- Haitian officials said they had killed a major gang leader in the capital as private mercenaries and at least 2,000 El Salvadoran troops join the fight to regain control of the troubled Caribbean nation. 
In a joint operation with other forces, Haiti’s National Police said they had attacked a gang stronghold in Cité Soleil and fatally wounded the leader of the “Boston” gang, Mathias Saintil, who died at a local hospital.
“One less gang leader,” Interim Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé wrote on X. “The gangs won’t be getting any sleep.”
Haiti’s gang crisis has drawn an array of international support, including the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force and a private military company run by Erik Prince, a former US Navy SEAL and founder of Blackwater. Prince suggested it was his contractors, known as the Task Force, and who work as a division within the national police, or HNP, that were responsible for the gang leader’s death. 
“Hail to the HNP Task Force,” he wrote on X in response to the Prime Minister’s message. “Nice shot.”
Haiti’s powerful gangs — which at some points have controlled more than 90% of the capital and forced more than 1.5 million people to flee their homes — are coming under increased pressure. 
Last month, after four El Salvadoran soldiers disappeared in Haiti and were presumed kidnapped, President Nayib Bukele began sending thousands of troops to the country and has vowed to crush the “wicked” gangs. 
On Wednesday he posted videos of El Salvadoran soldiers patrolling largely empty streets in Haiti. “It looks like the gangs don’t want to fight us,” he wrote on X.
Also last week, one of Haiti’s largest and most notorious gang leaders, Wilson Joseph of the 400 Marozo group, asked for the United Nations to establish peace talks.

At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
- Published
At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.
The Interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.
The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.
Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors.
Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued.
President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings.
In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys.
"We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said.
The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea.
Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored.
Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain.
Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria.
Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals.
More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities.
The Canary Islands have become a major entry point into Europe for migrants and refugees making the dangerous Atlantic crossing from West Africa.
The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean.
Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat.
Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency.
The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections.
In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries.

Trump tag-teams briefing room with UFC’s Dana White to field questions after bizarre job offer
Trump made a rare appearance at the White House briefing room lectern and introduced the MMA mogul a day after posting that he wanted him to be his next press secretary. He fielded questions on Pete Hegseth facing impeachment, the Iran war being rejected by voters and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang coming under fire for an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy

Donald Trump on Monday made a sudden and rare appearance in the White House briefing room, tag-teaming with his friend, UFC President Dana White, and taking questions from the press corps on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Iran war and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
The president has faced growing scrutiny since Republicans lost control of Congress in a crushing midterm election defeat nearly a week ago. To help take on the press during a blistering news cycle, Trump brought White into the briefing room after publicly offering him the vacant job of White House press secretary and then claiming it was just a joke after White was reported to have turned it down.
“I thought I'd bring Dane here because he loves the idea and I love the idea. The only thing is, we have other things we have to think about,” Trump told reporters Monday.
White was shocked when reporters actually started asking him questions.
It started with a softball from one reporter who asked whether Trump or his Democratic rival, former President Joe Biden, would win in a UFC cage match. White replied with a compliment to Trump, calling him “the toughest, most resilient human being that I’ve ever met in my entire life.”
When asked whether White declined the press secretary job, the UFC chief said, “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything.”
The role, which was once filled by Karoline Leavitt before she left at the end of August to spend more time with her family, was very briefly filled by Katie Zacharia, but she only lasted five days on the job.
On Monday, Trump explained his decision to offer White a spot at the lectern: “We were having a very bad press day...I don’t know why; I thought of his name. He’s been my friend for a long time. I said, ‘You know, I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary.’ I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding.”
Trump claimed the Iran war, which was a major factor in the GOP’s midterm shellacking after causing gas prices to soar, will be ending soon.
One reporter asked the president Thursday why not just declare the Iran war over now, given that he already claimed to have stopped the Middle Eastern country from having a nuclear weapon — his main objective of the conflict.
“We have some great allies there, and we have to make sure they're not hurt, and they would be hurt. They are right now a lot safer than they were six months ago, because Iran's been very much decapitated,” Trump said.
“But they're still the bully of the Middle East a little bit, and I see that. We want to make sure they're okay. We want to make sure it's a long-term solution, not just a short-term.”
Trump also defended Hegseth, who has been unwavering in his support of the war, as Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican and staunch critic of the president, reintroduced articles of impeachment against the Pentagon chief.
The articles published Monday accuse Hegseth of “waging the Iran war despite no declaration of war, statutory authorization, attack on the United States, or imminent threat,” among other allegations.
Trump called Massie a “stone-cold loser” and then suggested that Hegseth is “winning the war” in Iran, which has raged on for more than eight months.
“He's certainly winning the war,” Trump said. “Iran would love to make a deal, and they've been obliterated.”
Trump was repeatedly asked about a newly revealed alleged affair that Huang, one of the president’s allies in the AI industry, had with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang admitted in a message to his company that he was “unfaithful to my wife” and took "full responsibility" for his actions.
It came afterThe New York Times reported that Huang had formed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data center that U.S. officials believe was feeding information to Beijing.
Nvidia announced Sunday that its board was opening an investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Trump said he was “amazed” by the news “because I view him as a very high quality person. I've known him a long time,” adding, “I hope there's no problem. I believe he's suffering greatly.”
The president said he spoke with Huang earlier Thursday, and the executive said he had “absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
When asked if he knew about Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese spy when he visited Beijing in May, Trump said, “No, I didn’t hear about it then.”

Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
- Published
Perched on a ridge high up in the spectacular scenery of the German Alps lie the burned-out ruins of a mountain house called The Eagle's Nest, which is now at the heart of an intense debate about Germany's Nazi past.
Known in German as Kehlsteinhaus, the retreat was built by the Nazis in 1938, and frequented by Adolf Hitler and other high-ranking Nazis and their guests. After World War Two it was classified as a historical monument recalling the Nazi era.
Last month it was gutted by fire in a suspected arson attack, and some believe it should be completely destroyed, the site returned to nature and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.
But others want it either partially or completely rebuilt, wary of the risk of turning it into a site for Neo-Nazi pilgrimage at a time when Germany is witnessing the resurgence of the far-right.
Germany has an "everlasting responsibility to communicate, to deal with our Nazi past", said Isabel Heinemann, professor of contemporary history at Munich's Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU).
But rebuilding the site completely, she warned, would mean putting "highly ideologised or highly ideological architecture" back in place.
Before it was burned down during the evening of 23 October, the Eagle's Nest had been a popular tourist attraction, owned by the state of Bavaria and operating for many years as a restaurant.
Visitors would take a bus and then ride the original brass and mirror-panelled lift through the mountain to the Kehlsteinhaus to savour the magnificent views above the town of Berchtesgaden.
Once there, they could eat sausages in the beer garden on the Obersalzberg at 1,834m (6,017ft) above sea level, overlooking the Alps.
Unlike Hitler's nearby summer residence, the Berghof, which was bombed in World War Two and demolished in 1952, the Eagle's Nest survived the war.
Tens of thousands of tourists visited each season, providing an important source of income to the region.
In the 1990s, amid concerns that the site did not do enough to confront the crimes of the Nazi past, a museum, the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, was opened close by.
Around 15 years ago, a photo exhibit was opened in the Kehlsteinhaus about its history.
Although the Eagle's Nest itself was "largely destroyed" by the fire, according to police, the documentation centre survived unscathed.
The authorities have not commented on a possible motive, but a 33-year-old man with a history of mental illness has been detained in a secure psychiatric hospital on suspicion of arson.
- Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat 
  - Published24 October
Some feel this is the moment to allow the site to fade into history.
"It's been torched now. It's been destroyed. I think they should just clear away the rubble and leave the mountain as it should be in its natural state," said Prof Sir Richard J. Evans, a specialist in Nazi Germany at the University of Cambridge.
That has happened with "quite a few other Nazi sites", he argued, including the bunker in Berlin where Hitler killed himself: "The bunker was filled in with concrete and a children's playground put on the top of it on the ground."
The Kehlsteinhaus was just "a Nazi vanity project" since romanticised by the name Eagle's Nest, he said.
But Bavaria's authorities take a different view about the site's future.
Both the state's interior minister, Joachim Herrmann, and its minister for the arts, Markus Blume, have spoken out in favour of rebuilding the Kehlsteinhaus.
"We can hardly leave a ruin standing there," Herrmann said.
Sven Keller, head of the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, believes it is important not to leave the site in ruins, as that could encourage Neo-Nazi pilgrims, who would be able to hike up there completely undisturbed.
"We have quite some experience at Obersalzberg with what happens if we clear those sites. Hitler's Berghof was demolished in the 1950s, and in our experience, this does not remove such sites from the mental maps of people," he told the BBC's Today programme.
Nor does he believe "a one-on-one reconstruction" of the site is possible, and Blume has made clear on Bavarian radio that "it should not and must not cost the taxpayer anything".
Herrmann said they would look for a sensible solution in consultation with historians, given the historically complex circumstances surrounding the building.
Heinemann, who also heads the Leibniz Institute for Contemporary History, believes full-scale reconstruction should be "out of the question".
"I rather think we can document the state left by the fire and also document the historical remains of the Kehlsteinhaus, and then reconstruct parts in a modern design, to make clear the different layers of time that can be seen in this building," she told the BBC.
Germany and Austria have long struggled to deal with the fraught legacy of buildings and sites connected to the Nazi era.
With the recent rise of the far-right AfD and the Austrian Freedom Party, the debate over Erinnerungskultur (Culture of Remembrance) has taken on a new urgency.
A row broke out recently in Germany when AfD and conservative CDU councillors in a town in Saxony decided to ban "stumbling stones" memorials - embedded small brass plaques in the streets - to victims of the Nazis.
In Austria over the summer, a police station was opened in the house where Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn. It followed years of controversy about how the house should be used.
The Austrian government said the police presence would help prevent neo-Nazi pilgrims.
But others had wanted the house to become a centre of responsibility, actively confronting the Nazi past.
As one resident of Braunau am Inn told me, it was a delicate balance between how much to remember and how much to forget.

A video circulating on social media purportedly shows External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar recounting how a Russian minister mocked him over the India-China border dispute, questioning India’s position on China before he advised Russia on its conflict with Ukraine. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar recounting how a Russian minister mocked him over the India-China border dispute.
Fact: The viral video is manipulated. It features an actual video of External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar speaking in Atlanta, US, about discussions on the Russia-Ukraine conflict at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting. The original audio has been replaced with fabricated remarks. The MEA Fact Check also flagged the viral video as fake. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
To verify whether External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar made any such statement, we searched Google using relevant keywords but found no credible news reports or official statements confirming the claim.
We also reviewed the official social media accounts of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) (here, here, and here) and S Jaishankar (here, here, and here) but found no mention of the alleged exchange or the remarks attributed to him.
We noticed that the viral video carries a watermark from the news agency ANI. A keyword search led us to an ANI post on X (archived), dated 01 November 2026, featuring the same footage of Jaishankar, wearing the same attire and speaking against an identical background. However, his actual remarks in the original video were entirely different. He was speaking in Atlanta, US, about the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting and discussions on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The viral clip has been manipulated, with fabricated audio added to the original footage.
Suspecting the video was doctored, we analysed it with multiple AI detection tools, including Hive AI and NVIDIA’s Synthetic Video Detector. Hive AI gave an aggregate score of 99.4%, indicating a high likelihood of AI-generated or manipulated content. NVIDIA’s detector also classified the footage as synthetic media.
The MEA Fact Check also debunked the claim in an X post (archived) dated 3 November 2026, flagging the viral video as fake and cautioning against the circulation of such malicious posts on social media.
To sum up, this viral video of External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar allegedly saying a Russian minister mocked him over the India-China border dispute is a deepfake.

The COVID-19 pandemic is having a devastating impact across the world. Efforts to contain the coronavirus are vital to the health of the world’s population, but they are also exposing children to increased risk of violence – including maltreatment, gender-based violence and sexual exploitation.
As leaders of organisations committed to ending violence against children, we come together in solidarity to share our deep concern, call for action and pledge our support to protect children from violence and reduce the impact of COVID-19 on children in every country and community.
A third of the global population is on COVID-19 lockdown, and school closures have impacted more than 1.5 billion children. Movement restrictions, loss of income, isolation, overcrowding and high levels of stress and anxiety are increasing the likelihood that children experience and observe physical, psychological and sexual abuse at home – particularly those children already living in violent or dysfunctional family situations. And while online communities have become central to maintain many children’s learning, support and play, it is also increasing their exposure to cyberbullying, risky online behavior and sexual exploitation.
The situation is aggravated by children’s lack of access to schoolfriends, teachers, social workers and the safe space and services that schools provide. The most vulnerable children – including refugees, migrants, and children who are internally displaced, deprived of liberty, living without parental care, living on the street and in urban slums, with disabilities, and living in conflict-affected areas – are a particular concern. For many, growing economic vulnerability will increase the threat of child labour, child marriage and child trafficking.
We must act now. Together, we call on governments, the international community and leaders in every sector to urgently respond with a united effort to protect children from the heightened risk of violence, exploitation and abuse as part of the broader response to COVID-19.
Governments have a central role to play. They must ensure that COVID-19 prevention and response plans integrate age appropriate and gender sensitive measures to protect all children from violence, neglect and abuse. Child protection services and workers must be designated as essential and resourced accordingly.
Working with and supporting governments, our collective response must include: maintaining essential health and social welfare services, including mental health and psychosocial support; providing child protection case management and emergency alternative care arrangements; ensuring social protection for the most vulnerable children and households; continuing care and protection for children in institutions; and communicating with and engaging parents, caregivers and children themselves with evidence-based information and advice. National helplines, school counsellors and other child-friendly reporting mechanisms enable children in distress to reach out for help, and must be adapted to the challenges of COVID-19.
Given the heightened risks of online harms, technology companies and telecoms providers must do everything they can to keep children safe online. This includes providing access to cost-free child helplines, age-appropriate services and safe e-education platforms - and using their platforms to share child online safety advice. They must also do more to detect and stop harmful activity against children online, including grooming and the creation and distribution of child sexual abuse images and videos.
As global organisations working to end violence against children, we will continue to advocate for and invest in effective child protection solutions. We will collectively develop and share technical resources and guidance for policymakers, practitioners, parents, caregivers and children themselves. And we will support the courageous health, child protection and humanitarian professionals working around the clock to keep children safe during these unprecedented times.
In recent years, the global community has made significant gains in protecting children from violence. We must not allow those gains to be lost during the current turmoil. We must do all we can to keep children safe now. And we must plan ahead together, so that once the immediate health crisis is over, we can get back on track towards the goal of ending all forms of violence, abuse and neglect of children

The Paramount+ and HBO Max marriage is around the corner.
Skydance will bundle the streamers in early 2027, the company said Monday as it shared its third-quarter earnings — its first report since Paramount bought Warner Bros. Discovery in early October.
It's unclear how much the HBO Max-Paramount+ bundle will cost. Skydance said it would share more details on the bundle and "its streaming roadmap" in the coming months.
HBO Max costs $10.99 a month with ads, or $18.49 for the standard ad-free plan, while Paramount+ is $8.99 a month with ads and $13.99 for the ad-free version.
Without a discount, it costs about $20 a month to get HBO Max and Paramount+ with ads separately, and $32.48 to get them without ads.
David Ellison's media giant is also planning to combine the Paramount+ and HBO Max tech platforms in the next 11 months so it can create a "unified product."
Paramount merged the backend of its namesake streamer with its free service, Pluto TV, over about 18 months in a process known internally as convergence.
Skydance said it will lean on AI tools to move faster this time around.
"We expect to bring Paramount+ and HBO Max together much faster, aiming to align our backend systems within a year of closing, enabling us to quickly deliver a unified product," Skydance said in its third-quarter shareholder letter.
Skydance posted solid Q3 earnings
Skydance largely met Wall Street's expectations in its third-quarter report. The new media company met its revenue projections and exceeded adjusted earnings estimates.
Revenue climbed 5% year-over-year to $7 billion, within the $6.95 billion to $7.15 billion range that Paramount had told investors to expect.
Adjusted EBITDA, a measure of profitability excluding certain items, was $1 billion, above the company's $875 million to $975 million range.
Shares were volatile in early after-hours trading, following a surge of over 8.5% on Monday. Skydance's stock entered earnings down more than 11% since the October 6 merger.

Sunil Sharma said, "In barely two weeks, Jammu has witnessed two devastating market fires: first at Shiv Market near the Railway Station and now at Nehru Market. These are not just shops; they represent the livelihoods of hundreds of families. Traders cannot be sent home with mere words of sympathy. They need relief on the ground and a concrete plan to ensure that such incidents do not happen again."
In consultation with Party State President Sat Sharma MP (Rajya Sabha), Sunil Sharma announced the constitution of a six-member committee headed by MLA Sham Lal Sharma (Jammu North), comprising Dr. Narinder Singh, MLAs Yudhvir Sethi, Vikram Randhawa and Arvind Gupta, and Party General Secretary Baldev Singh Billowria.
The committee will assess the losses suffered by traders at both Nehru Market and Shiv Market and prepare a comprehensive list of affected traders. It will subsequently take up the matter with the Government to ensure time-bound relief and rehabilitation. The committee will also pursue the demand for allowing MLAs to utilise their Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to extend assistance to the affected traders.
Sharma demanded adequate and time-bound compensation for the affected traders of both markets, over and above the routine relief norms, keeping in view the extent of losses suffered by them.
He also called for the deployment of additional fire tenders in the Warehouse area, including compact fire tenders and quick response vehicles capable of entering narrow market lanes, to ensure their availability near Jammu's crowded commercial areas.
Emphasising the need for long term preventive measures, he urged the Government to identify and allot a separate, isolated site for warehouses and the storage of inflammable goods, away from crowded markets and residential areas.
Referring to the earlier fire incident at Shiv Market, Sunil Sharma said, "After the Shiv Market fire, the NC Government promised 'all possible assistance', but no relief amount or timeline has been made public so far. The Omar Government must now move from assurances to action."
Sunil Sharma reiterated that the affected traders deserve immediate relief, fair compensation and proper rehabilitation, and stressed that the Government must take concrete and time-bound steps to address their concerns and strengthen fire safety arrangements across Jammu's commercial establishments.

A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”
The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters.
A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. It is the first case involving a British national contracting Ebola in the current outbreak.
The Royal Free hospital in London has a high-level isolation unit for infectious diseases such as Ebola; other centres are in Newcastle and Liverpool.
Ebola is a highly contagious, severe and often fatal illness. It is spread through direct contact with body fluids such as the blood or vomit of infected people, or dead bodies.
The current outbreak, declared on 15 May by DR Congo’s health ministry, has surpassed 10,000 cases, and 5,000 deaths. It is the 17th in DR Congo since Ebola was identified, was caused by the Bundibugyo virus, and has become the largest and deadliest in the country’s history. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved treatment, though vaccine trials are under way.
Since the outbreak started, it has spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last month Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus. She, along with a close contact, were evacuated to Switzerland for treatment.
In an interview with the Guardian last month, Dr Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), said the “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak meant it could reach the UK and other countries.
“We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said. “Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.
“It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented.”
Other patients who have been medically evacuated for specialised care since the start of the outbreak include two sent to Germany and one to the Netherlands. Another case was reported in France in July.
British health authorities say the risk to the wider public from imported Ebola cases remains low and the NHS has procedures in place to manage suspected and confirmed infections.
There have only been four confirmed cases recorded in Britain since 1976, according to the UK Health Security Agency.

FSSAI seizes food items worth ₹81.8 crore, suspends over 1,100 licences in two-month enforcement drive
The food safety regulator said it had inspected 56,431 establishments and issued 10,047 improvement notices from September 1 to November 5 as part of the drive.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) led an intensive nationwide inspection drive from September 1 to November 5, during which it seized more than 3,270 metric tonnes of food products worth an estimated ₹81.80 crore and suspended more than 1,100 licences.
In a series of posts on X, the food safety regulator said it had inspected 56,431 establishments and issued 10,047 improvement notices as part of the enforcement drive held across States and Union Territories in collaboration with State Food Safety Authorities.
52 licences cancelled, 314 establishments sealed
It also collected 43,939 samples, of which 23,648 had been analysed. Out of these analysed samples, 2,273 were found to be non-compliant with prescribed food safety standards. The seized food products that were found to be non-compliant with safety standards included oils, milk, paneer, sweets, ghee, bakery items, chocolates, ice cream, namkeen, packaged food and festive hampers.
Highlighting the scale of the operation, the FSSAI said it had suspended 1,133 licences and cancelled the licences of 52 food establishments. Additionally, it also sealed 314 establishments and initiated 410 prosecutions.
"Through rigorous checks on over 56,000 food establishments, authorities took decisive action against substandard practices, issuing over 10,000 improvement notices and suspending more than 1,100 licences to maintain uncompromising safety standards," it said.
The regulator said it would continue working with State Food Safety Authorities to ensure "greater adherence to prescribed food safety standards across the food ecosystem".
FSSAI action on food safety violations
This year, the FSSAI had stepped up its crackdown on food safety violations by investigating multiple eateries and e-commerce companies. Earlier, it banned the sale of Nestle's “Low Fat Dairy Whitener” after a sample of the product taken from The Lalit hotel in New Delhi's Connaught Place was declared to be “unsafe” and “substandard”.
The latest findings highlight the scale of action taken during the festive season, with FSSAI expected to continue inspections and monitoring to ensure businesses follow food safety regulations.
Last month, the body issued a directive to food safety authorities across all states and union territories to step up surveillance and enforcement actions against unsafe food products ahead of the festive season. This directive was aimed at curbing the circulation of “adulterated, counterfeited and unsafe food products”.
