Tiny Computer (USD 3.99): Unfolding Retro computer feels
Imagine getting a vintage PC feel on something as new and pristine as the iPhone Duo? That is exactly what the app Tiny Computer can deliver. Using the half-fold setting of the iPhone Duo, the app turns your phone into a proper vintage computer. The upper half of the screen becomes the display while the lower half becomes the keyboard. You get to choose from ten different computers in total, including the Apple Macintosh, IBM PC, iMac G3, IBM ThinkPad, Windows XP, Amiga 500, and more.
It is not just all show; you can actually use some retro paint apps, run old command-line interfaces, play games like Solitaire, and even type on clicky keyboards. Each machine also hides secret commands and files paired with occasional crashes to make the whole experience even more believable.
Deck Man (USD 4.99): Go cassette crazy!
Another app that brings retro feels to the Duo is the Deck Man. It is one of the most visually appealing apps for the Duo because it essentially turns your iPhone Duo into a 1980s cassette Walkman player. The app uses the unfolded version of the phone as the collection of cassettes in your music library that you can browse. You then “insert” the cassette of your choice into the deck, and once you fold it, the secondary screen mimics the look of a cassette Walkman player.
The app has realistic mechanical clicks, background tape static, and if you fast-forward or rewind it too aggressively, the virtual tape inside can get all tangled and then would have to be untangled manually, just like a retro cassette player. “Tape” this one to your Duo!
MD Vinyl (Free): Spin those discs!
If cassettes are “too” modern for you, then you can go even further back in the music era with the iPhone Duo by installing MD Vinyl. This essentially turns the Duo into a virtual turntable with spinning records and album art. The record design determines the aesthetics of the app. The app allows you to pick and drop the needle to play or pause the tracks. It can pair with music apps like Apple Music and Spotify. It is not a new app and has existed for years, but it attains a whole new dimension on the Duo, adding a vintage touch to the modern audio experience.
Fold Accordion (USD 2.99): Fold and unfold to create music
If there is one app that makes the most use of the iPhone Duo’s form factor, it is the Fold Accordion. It literally turns the hinge of the iPhone Duo into working accordion bellows. When you launch the app, it places the keys on the display, which you can press with your right hand while opening and closing the Duo with the left hand to create music of your own. The app comes with a learning mode which highlights keys you have to press to create something pleasant, instead of getting straight to the chaos of keys. A great way to test that folding mechanism too.
Delta (Nintendo DS) (free): Double screen gaming magic, DS style!
Popular Retro Game emulator Delta has launched an updated version of its app, specifically for the iPhone Duo. The app brings specially designed skins for the iPhone Duo, and the most interesting one of the lot is the Nintendo DS portable gaming console, which interestingly was the world’s first mainstream foldable device. The app uses the inner display of the iPhone Duo to bring a DS-style layout and controls across the displays. The game even enters sleep state when the device is folded, similar to the Nintendo DS. Trust the Duo to bring back the magic of double-screen gaming.
Toastie (USD 2.99): Smartest thing since sliced bread!
Unleash the inner chef in you with the absolutely useless but equally fun app called Toastie. This app turns the iPhone Duo into a – wait for it – virtual grilled cheese toaster. You get 15 seconds to assemble your sandwich, and once you are done, you have to hit the ‘grill’ button and physically close the iPhone Duo shut. You then have to wait, listen to the sizzle, or get a slight peek to ensure your toastie is grilling well. If you open the phone too soon, the cheese won’t be melted; if you wait too long, it might end up getting burned. Once you are done with it, you serve it, and you get a star based on your accuracy, recipe, timing, and so on. Useful? Not. But definitely the smartest thing since sliced bread. Actually, the smartest thing done to sliced bread!
TypeDraw (USD 4.99): Paper-like Moleskine
The iPhone Duo looks like a handy pocket notebook or a passport, and TypeDraw literally converts it into a handy little Moleskine-like notebook. It even comes with a digital thread, just like you find on a notebook, which you have to move or swipe aside to open the notebook (or just open the Duo). You can write anywhere on a page using an Apple Pencil or your finger and can even fiddle and curl up paper corners, as well as choose fonts (you can convert your handwriting into one, if you wish), types of paper, and even plain, ruled, dotted, or grid patterns on paper. And the page turns on the internal display are absolutely paper-like. It is like carrying a real notebook.
Snapshots ($1.99): Unfold to Polaroid
Snapshots is an app that helps your Duo morph into an instant camera. It is one of the very first community-developed apps optimized specifically for the iPhone Duo. When bent in half (90 degrees), the top half of the primary display becomes the viewfinder while the bottom half holds the controls. Once you hit the shutter, the photo captured on the upper half of the viewfinder is virtually printed on the lower half with the same mechanical sound and effect as on an instant camera. Just like with a real instant camera, the photo does not appear right away but takes a few seconds to develop, giving us those Polaroid feels.
Phridge (free): Chill…literally!
This is perhaps the most quirky and our personal favorite app in the list. It turns the iPhone Duo into a – wait for it – refrigerator. When folded, you can decorate the ‘door’ of this fridge with magnets, to-do lists, photographs. And when you open it, you can see groceries and food and drink inside and arrange them. This is when the real fun happens, because you can topple something over, drop a fizzy drink, or break a glass jar or bottle. You can also place your hand in a slingshot to shoot stones at the shelves, or get a sword to slice things in half, if you feel like some chaos. You can only close the fridge when you fold the phone shut, making the hinge integral to its operation. How cool is that? Just chillin…
Chompduo (Free): Jaw-dropping (and closing) stuff!
We all need an app that adds six hungry monsters to your iPhone Duo. Well, we do, anyway. That is exactly what ChompDuo does. When installed, it unleashes six hungry monsters on your Duo that open their huge mouths when the device is unfolded, making the inner display a giant mouth. You can tap on the open mouth to make it bite or drag it to squeeze it shut. When you fold the phone, the jaws close shut with a chomp sound, and a pair of googly eyes appear on the outer display, which can jump when you tap on them. What more does one need on a foldable?

The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at three premises linked to crypto exchanges CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India (DEI) over alleged unauthorised cross-border transactions involving crypto derivatives and tokenised foreign stocks. In a statement, the agency said the searches were conducted between November 4 and November 5 across Bengaluru. The crypto trading transactions in question run into thousands of crores of Rupees, as per ED. “ED Bengaluru has conducted search(es) at three premises linked to Neblio Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (CoinDCX parent) and Excelium Technologies Pvt. Ltd.(which operates Delta Exchange India) under FEMA 1999 in the case of large scale unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto token derivatives and real world asset tokens,” said ED in a statement. As per the directorate, ED began its probe into the matter after receiving information of alleged forex violations by CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India. The agency alleged that CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India facilitated spot trading, futures and options (F&O) trading and trading in tokenised shares of foreign companies – all through cryptocurrencies. ED also claimed CoinDCX advertised these products despite not being authorised to offer them. While CoinDCX is yet to issue a statement on the matter, Delta Exchange India said that it cooperated “fully” with the officials and furnished the information sought. In a post on X, the crypto exchange further claimed that it is not involved in “any cross-border transfer of VDAs (virtual digital assets) in any form or manner”. “We acknowledge the Enforcement Directorate’s statement regarding their visit to our premises on 4th & 5th November… We cooperated fully with the officials and provided the information that they sought. We remain committed to extending our support and cooperation as may be required…,” said Delta Exchange India. CoinDCX's Alleged Modus Operandi According to the ED, user funds (deposited in Rupees) were allegedly converted into stablecoins, primarily USDT, and then transferred to overseas crypto platforms including Binance, KuCoin, Gate.io and Bybit. The agency alleged that these transfers circumvented forex rules governing cross-border money transfers. For spot trades, the ED alleged that CoinDCX used an account, opened in the name of a Costa Rica-based entity, to send the USDT to foreign crypto platforms. Describing the Costa Rican company as a mere “paper entity”, the agency alleged that the transactions were allegedly actually executed directly through CoinDCX APIs. The directorate also made similar allegations for CoinDCX’s F&O product. ED said that the homegrown platform allegedly opened matching positions via APIs on foreign platforms after users placed orders, with settlements occurring overseas when positions were closed. The ED also claimed that tokenised-stock trading on CoinDCX was routed through Hyperliquid, an overseas decentralised crypto trading platform. It said that user funds were converted into USDT to open positions, with settlements completed on the overseas platform. The alleged volumes of spot, derivatives and tokenised-stock transactions were described as running into thousands of crores of rupees. The ED also alleged that CoinDCX paid hundreds of crores in transaction fees to foreign platforms in stablecoins. This, the agency said, contravened forex rules. Delta Exchange India Under ED Radar Just like CoinDCX, the Enforcement Directorate also alleged that Delta Exchange India offered spot trading, crypto derivatives and tokenised foreign stocks via cryptocurrencies. It alleged that a large volume of DEI’s derivatives and tokenised-stock transactions was routed through CoinDCX, which in turn executed them on foreign platforms. The agency alleged that Delta Exchange India also transferred hundreds of crores of Rupees to overseas associate entities. These transfers are under investigation, added the ED. In a statement, the ED said the fintech products offered by both crypto exchanges appear to have prima facie contravened norms under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the SEBI Act, 1992 and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The investigation remains ongoing. The searches are part of ED’s broader clampdown on forex violations involving crypto platforms. Just days ago, the directorate launched a probe into alleged FEMA violations involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform, Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr. Prior to this in June this year, the ED had also searched six premises linked to five platforms, namely Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta, over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.

Revised Maximum Retail Prices (MRPs) of 1,364 anti-cancer formulations have come into effect from Monday (November 9, 2026), a move projected to save consumers an estimated ₹3,540.38 crore annually, according to an official release.
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), functioning under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, capped trade margins on the MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs based on recommendations submitted on October 17, 2026, by an Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
Also read | Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
According to the Ministry, 85 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations across 121 drugs as of November 8, 2026.
Price reductions of over 50% have been reported for 679 brands, with the highest price cut recorded at 96.45%, the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers: Department of Pharmaceuticals said in the release.
The Ministry stated that no chemist or hospital pharmacy is permitted to charge more than the revised MRP.
Consumers can verify medicine rates via the revised MRP printed on packs, the 'Pharma Sahi Daam' mobile application, or the official NPPA website (nppa.gov.in), it said.

The year 2026 has been a breakthrough for action RPGs. We have already had the likes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Control Resonant performing beyond expectations. However, gamers had been waiting for one action RPG, and it was Phantom Blade Zero. The game had captured everyone’s imagination with incredibly fluid and impactful combat during its multiple showcases.
So, did Phantom Blade Zero meet its promised hype? After playing almost 40 hours of Phantom Blade Zero, I can most definitely say that it has the best combat I have seen in any recent action RPG releases, but sadly that’s not the entire picture. Here is our Phantom Blade Zero review to help you know whether the game is worth playing or not.
Combat Straight Out of a Fever Dream
Phantom Blade Zero doesn’t take long to send you right into action. From the very beginning, you get to experience what the absolute peak of the game’s combat can do when Soul fights his brother in the prologue, one of the earliest Phantom Blade Zero bosses. The game gives a fully powered Soul to players and allows them to fight Zuo Shang, the Shadow Sovereign.
Although Soul constantly regenerates HP to avoid losing during this fight, it lets us see the full potential of the combat at a very early stage, also acting as the perfect hook for the game. The combat is very energetic and is unlike anything I have played before. It feels straight out of a Shaolin or Kung Fu movie, and Donnie Yen’s touch is clearly noticeable in every movement.
The closest combat to Phantom Blade Zero I have seen is in Black Desert Online, but that’s only in terms of visuals. In terms of responsiveness for high-speed combat, Phantom Blade Zero is in a class of its own, untouched by any other game.
Parry, Parry, and Parry
From a distance, the combat can seem spammy, but when you actually play the game, every movement, parry, dodge, and block requires precision. Even though enemy attacks feel too fast at a glance, the combination of sound makes it feel trackable, allowing you to parry without feeling unfair.
And parrying in Phantom Blade Zero is absolutely spot on. The constant ringing sound of parrying and blocking in every boss fight will make any action RPG fun and ecstatic. The last time I had this much fun was while playing Sekiro, but even then, parrying in Phantom Blade Zero feels like a whole other level of enjoyment.
Combos Straight Out of a Fighting Game
But the game is not all about parrying. It also features combo attacks, different for every weapon. The combos in Phantom Blade Zero are very similar to fighting games, but a tad bit less complicated. Although you can win the game without using any combos, once you have mastered it, the combat reaches an entirely different level.
Pulling off powerful combos can literally destroy an enemy’s health bar or allow you to apply specific stat effects much quicker. One combo I loved using throughout the second half of the game was Fiend Saw’s, which applies Fiend Aura erosion.
However, it’s not just the statistical aspect when it comes to combos; I largely did it in fights because it looked extremely cool. Combos on every weapon have unique animations, some of which look so extraordinary that I was even willing to ignore the damage drop, if any, to perform them.
A Weapon Arsenal That Makes Every Other Game Ashamed
Ever since I finished Elden Ring, I had never expected to see another game introduce that many weapons with unique abilities. Weapons in Phantom Blade Zero have gone beyond that, not only having unique abilities, but also having unique animations for each. The best part about the weapons is that you directly obtain most of them by defeating bosses. So, you are basically taking their weapon after defeating them.
There are over 55 weapons in Phantom Blade Zero, and each weapon having its own identity is truly unbelievable. Players can carry two weapons at the same time, while also having a third Phantom Edge. Letting players freely swap between these is another expert addition to the combat that feels incredibly satisfying to perform.
Another thing to note is that every weapon has specific effects and abilities. These abilities get stronger the more you upgrade the weapons. Some abilities completely change how you fight with the weapon. For example, the Fanatic’s Broken Blade can get you drunk for 20 seconds, literally, completely changing your combat style until you sober up. And there are countless other examples.
An Interesting Story Plagued by Subpar Voice Acting
Phantom Blade Zero tells a story inspired by Chinese mythology. After playing Black Myth Wukong, I was extremely excited to have a similar level of immersion from this game. The story starts with a fight between Soul and his brother, who end up piercing each other’s hearts.
Soul has been falsely accused of assassinating the leader of the Order, which is why he is fighting his brother and rival, who now acts as the Shadow Sovereign. After dying, the Flesh Sculptor offers a new heart to Soul, which only allows him to live for 66 days. Within this time, Soul has to find the mastermind behind the assassination, while fighting his former allies.
Sounds interesting, right? Sadly, that entire notion fell flat just 20 minutes into the game. The reason was the subpar English voice acting in the game.
Most of the English voice acting in Phantom Blade Zero literally felt emotionless. Only very few characters actually did a good job. Compared to Black Myth Wukong, which had incredible voice acting for every character, Phantom Blade Zero was a big letdown.
And sadly, the voice acting also ruined my experience of the game’s story. Although the essence of Phantom Blade Zero’s story feels great, especially the connecting lore in the game, I couldn’t be bothered to pay too much attention to it.
And that’s coming from a person who loves getting into the lore of any game he likes. However, for anyone who understands Chinese, you may have a better experience than I did because the Chinese dub sounded much better.
Exploration is Expansive but Comes with Too Much Handholding
Phantom Blade Zero is a linear game, but most of its levels are very open-ended. The map has multiple regions, each being an open level. However, even though the levels are open, the pathways are fairly linear, so not a lot of parkour is possible. Even then, the game does have some hidden nooks and quests.
The best part about it is that the game forces you to return to older maps, as new keys or quests are obtained later down the line that open specific segments of older areas. Even story missions change regions. Reaching a specific point in the story can turn all the NPCs you have met in previous maps into enemies when you return.
Some guards who blocked you from certain sections would then become defeatable to unlock the area.
However, Phantom Blade Zero does too much handholding in exploration that I personally dislike. Almost every detail that you even cross over without noticing would appear on the map. This often kills the ‘exploration through eyes.’ If everything appears on the map, what’s the need to actually look for it yourself?
Enemies and Bosses Are All Teeth and No Bite
Phantom Blade Zero has an incredible cast of enemies and bosses. Although the normal enemies don’t have that much variety overall, they have some unique personalities that make them stand out. Like the puppets in Village of Lu, who throw their heads at you as attacks.
The bosses, on the other hand, are pure spectacles. Every boss fight is a well-animated action movie sequence, with Soul and the enemy going at each other no holds barred. Unfortunately, even though the fight looks and feels good, it never ends up becoming too challenging.
This can be a good thing for traditional action RPG players who are never into too much difficulty, but for soulslike players like me, the game can feel very easy at times. Excluding a couple of bosses, most of the fights only take one or two tries to finish.
Even at the Hellwalker Phantom Blade Zero difficulty, the game never felt too challenging. Normally, I wouldn’t have paid too much attention to this. However, S-Game had marketed their Hellwalker mode as a challenging alternative for hardcore players, with more boss movesets and better AI. That, I personally think, did not live up to my expectations.
Another reason for the boss fights to feel too easy is that bosses actually retain their second or third phases after your death. So, instead of redoing the fight from scratch, if you have finished the first phase, you can directly start fighting in the second phase with full heals after dying. Also, any enemies killed in the overworld remain dead.
I don’t think either of these things are bad. They provide a different experience from games of this genre. The enemy not respawning factor also helps greatly in exploration, as you truly get a feeling of 100% clearing an area.
Performance: Phantom Blade Zero Runs Smoothly, but Clips A Lot
The impactful and fluid combat of Phantom Blade Zero would have ended up being a complete disaster if the game didn’t run as smoothly as it does. Even at ultra graphics with DLSS turned off, I was comfortably getting above 50 FPS in combat. With DLSS set to quality, the FPS went up to 120+.
With Frame Generation set to 4x, I was getting above 180 FPS with no latency. However, when changing Frame Generation to 6x, the latency becomes very noticeable, so you’d better avoid it.
My Setup:
CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900x
CPU Cooler: CORSAIR H150 RGB
Motherboard: GIGABYTE B650M Gaming X AX
GPU: MSI Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
RAM: 32GB (32GB x 1) ADATA XPG DDR5 5600FSB LANCER
SSD: 1TB AORUS Gen 4 5000E NVMe storage
Monitor: 1080p @165hz
Although the game runs extremely well, it does have a fair bit of clunk and glitches. The terrain can often be a big issue, as you will find yourself constantly getting stuck on even a slightly protruding stone. For a game that has such good combat movement, it can feel very odd to have such basic issues.
Also, sometimes a level’s or cutscene assets can take time to load. But it was rare enough that I didn’t end up having a bad feeling. In terms of graphics, the game looks gorgeous. Some of the locations in the game are extremely scenic and can make you want to wait there for eternity.
Verdict: Phantom Blade Zero is a New Standard for the Action RPG Genre
Phantom Blade Zero is unparalleled in action combat, leaving behind all its competitors, whether in the past, present, or even in the coming future. Featuring over 55 unique weapons, each providing a unique playstyle, paired with an incredible number of cinematic boss fights, the game has completely left me mind-boggled and impressed.
However, it also suffers from terrible English voice acting, making players detached from the main story and the incredible visuals it offers. Alongside that, the game can feel very easy for soulslike players, but it also allows the game to be more accessible for others who simply prefer playing normal action RPGs.
Phantom Blade Zero overall is a masterfully crafted game that will grab you from the first parry, and won’t leave you until you have performed over a thousand different combos to get every possible achievement in the game. It is a true testament to how incredible and impactful combat can feel in the coming age of gaming.
So, that’s our Phantom Blade Zero review. What’s your opinion so far of the game? Let us know in the comments section below.

In late October and early November, a photo circulated on social media supposedly showing U.S. President Donald Trump, late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and singer Beyoncé aboard a private jet. The image shows Trump and Epstein sitting shirtless next to each other, with Beyoncé standing behind them.
"The Epstein files have leaked again !! As Jeffrey Epstein, Trump and Beyonce are all seen chilling on board," one X post (archived) captioned the image.
(X user @TomthunkitsMind)
The image spread primarily on X and Facebook.
In short, the photograph wasn't real. We didn't find it in any reputable news outlets and AI-detection tools indicated it was artificially generated. Google Gemini detected a watermark showing that the image was created or edited using Google AI. As such, we have rated the image fake.
How we know the image is fake
First, we didn't find the image in news outlets or any other credible sources — it spread solely on social media. If it were real, it would likely have been widely reported by news organizations. Another sign that the image was fake was Trump's physical appearance, as he looked much older than he did when Epstein was still alive.
Moreover, an analysis using Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, determined with 99.8% confidence that the image was "likely to be AI-generated."
(X user @TomthunkitsMind, Hive Moderation)
We also ran the image through Google Gemini's SynthID check, a tool that scans for watermarks embedded by artificial intelligence software. That scan detected a SynthID watermark and concluded, "this image contains a SynthID watermark, which indicates that it was generated or edited with Google AI."
(Google Gemini)
Readers who want to check whether an image contains a SynthID watermark can do so by uploading the photo to Google Gemini and asking, "Does this image have a SynthID watermark?" However, the absence of a SynthID watermark does't automatically mean an image is authentic, as it could have been created using other AI tools.
It's unclear who created the image, but it has circulated online at least since Oct. 26.
Some social media users sharing the image suggested Beyoncé was involved in Epstein's crimes. While the singer's name does appear in the Epstein Library, the references we found don't accuse her of any wrongdoing and, for example, concern such matters as tickets to her concerts:
(www.justice.gov/epstein)
(www.justice.gov)
All in all, while genuine photographs of Trump and Epstein together exist, the image above isn't real. It's one of many fabricated images of the two that have circulated on social media.

India’s anaemia burden is not in doubt. The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) found that more than half of women and about two-thirds of young children are anaemic. In this context, double-fortified salt (DFS) — fortified with iodine and iron — is often proposed as a potentially transformative solution. However, the case for DFS rests on convenience: everyone consumes salt, so why not add iron to it? But convenience is not efficacy, and a policy that asks the country to continue consuming salt to deliver iron deserves closer scrutiny.
Iron fortification of salt is a vehicle that cuts against public health. Indians consume, by most estimates, roughly twice the five grams of salt a day recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). About one in three adults has hypertension, and India’s own non-communicable disease (NCD) action plan commits to a 30% relative reduction in salt intake.

Insurtech Go Digit reported a 31.1% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹142.4 Cr from ₹206.8 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. The insurtech major's profit also declined 62.4% sequentially from ₹378.61 Cr in the June quarter. The decline in profitability came despite a marginal increase in insurance revenue, which rose 1.7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr during the quarter from ₹2,674.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, insurance revenue increased 2.1% from ₹2,665.6 Cr. Segment-wise, Motor Third Party (TP) insurance remained Go Digit's largest business, contributing ₹1,066.1 Cr to insurance revenue in Q2 FY27, up 8.3% YoY. Motor Own Damage (OD) insurance revenue grew at a faster pace of 11.4% YoY to ₹640.64 Cr. The company's gross written premium for the quarter dipped by 3.6% YoY to ₹2,571 Cr while gross direct premium, dipped 1.2% to ₹2,351 Cr. However, the company's insurance service result, which reflects the profitability of its insurance operations before investment and other financial income, sunk 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr from ₹161.98 Cr in the year-ago quarter. The figure also fell 62.3% sequentially from ₹114 Cr. The deterioration in the insurance service result came as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% YoY to ₹2,607.73 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,130.85 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Incurred claims rose 9.2% to ₹1,968.03 Cr from ₹1,802.96 Cr, while employee benefit expenses increased 4.3% to ₹95.48 Cr. Commission expenses, on the other hand, declined 2.6% YoY to ₹781.88 Cr from ₹803.10 Cr. Other insurance service expenses increased 1.7% to ₹94.52 Cr. On the investment front, Go Digit reported a 20.6% YoY increase in investment income to ₹368.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹305.5 Cr in the year-ago period. However, investment income declined 39.2% sequentially from ₹606.47 Cr. The company's net finance result, which includes investment income and insurance finance income or expenses, increased 28.6% YoY to ₹196.94 Cr. Consequently, Go Digit's profit before tax (PBT) declined 31.2% YoY to ₹190.18 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹276.30 Cr in Q2 FY26. The figure was also down 62.4% sequentially from ₹505.96 Cr in Q1 FY27. Total tax expense stood at ₹47.79 Cr during the quarter, comprising current tax of ₹3.93 Cr and deferred tax of ₹43.86 Cr. This compared with a total tax expense of ₹69.51 Cr in Q2 FY26. For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Go Digit reported a 3.2% YoY decline in net profit to ₹521 Cr from ₹538.23 Cr in H1 FY26. Insurance revenue increased 4.5% YoY to ₹5,386.09 Cr during the six-month period. Shares of Go Digit ended today’s trading session 1.05% higher at ₹260.30.

This 1,000 ft ocean liner once carried world leaders. Now it's being sunk deliberately
Authorities in Okaloosa County have confirmed their plan to sink the SS United States

A legendary ocean liner that once carried world leaders, Hollywood icons and thousands of immigrants across the Atlantic is preparing for a final journey to the floor of the Gulf of Mexico, where it will become the world’s largest artificial reef.
Over the weekend, authorities in Florida’s Okaloosa County confirmed the plan is to sink the SS United States on November 12, weather permitting, targeting a location roughly 22 nautical miles (41 kilometers) southwest of Destin and 32 nautical miles (59 kilometers) southeast of Pensacola.
The vessel will be towed from Alabama to the deployment site in the days prior, with deployment operations scheduled to begin at 10am.
"This is an exciting move forward to create a one-of-a-kind resource for the environment and for our tourism industry," county officials wrote in a news release.
Measuring nearly 1,000 feet (305 meters) in length — more than 100 feet (30 meters) longer than the RMS Titanic — the vessel stands as a mid-century engineering milestone and was also designed to double as a military troopship.
The ocean liner shattered the transatlantic speed record during its maiden voyage in 1952, averaging over 41 mph (66 kph) at 36 knots. It completed the crossing in three days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes, cutting 10 hours off the record held by the RMS Queen Mary.
To this day, the SS United States retains the transatlantic speed record for a passenger ship.
The ocean liner spent nearly three decades docked along the Delaware River in Philadelphia while preservationists sought options to restore it.
However, ambitious restoration projects were repeatedly abandoned due to steep costs. A prolonged legal conflict over dockage fees and rent between the nonprofit managing the vessel and its landlord eventually resulted in a court order requiring the ship to vacate its pier.
Following a 12-day journey under tow in March, the vessel arrived at the Port of Mobile in Alabama, where workers have spent months stripping away wiring, glass, plastic, and hazardous chemicals to prepare the structure for the water.
Although a preservation group called the New York Coalition filed a lawsuit in Pensacola federal court aiming to block the sinking on historical grounds, local leaders maintain that turning the vessel into a reef is the only viable alternative to sending it to a scrap yard.
"The SS United States has inspired millions the world over as a symbol of American pride and excellence," said Susan Gibbs, president of the SS United States Conservancy, the nonprofit working to preserve the vessel.
"Should the ship be converted into an artificial reef, she will become a unique historic attraction above and below the waterline."
The project is part of a $10.1 million commitment by Okaloosa County to acquire, transport, clean, and submerge the vessel, including $1 million earmarked for an onshore museum showcasing the ship's history.
A regional funding partnership helped secure the final deployment location: Pensacola tourism officials contributed $1.5 million, while Coastal Conservation Association Florida added $500,000—marking the largest single donation in the organization's 40-year history.
"This collaboration will foster amazing adventures for generations of visitors and create a tourism economy that will benefit the state and the entire Northwest Florida region," Okaloosa County Board Chairman Paul Mixon said in a statement.
Once submerged, the SS United States will join more than 500 artificial reefs in Okaloosa County, including a dozen smaller shipwrecks.
Resting at a seabed depth of approximately 180 feet (55 meters), the vessel's upper decks will sit roughly 60 feet (18 meters) below the surface, making the reef accessible to both novice and experienced scuba divers. The site is also 12 nautical miles (22 kilometers) from the USS Oriskany, an aircraft carrier sunk as a dive site in 2006.
"To have an opportunity to have the SS United States right here by our shore is a heritage and a legacy that is generational," said Okaloosa County Commissioner Mel Ponder. "I’m very excited for not only what it does for the diving community, but also the fishing community, but the community at large."
Local businesses, including scuba outlets, charter fishing fleets, and hotels, expect the marine destination to generate millions of dollars annually in tourism revenue while providing critical new marine habitats.
"The transformation of the SS United States into the world’s largest artificial reef creates a rare opportunity to elevate our entire region on the global stage," said Darien Schaefer, president and CEO of Visit Pensacola.
"It is truly a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to contribute to the creation of the world’s largest artificial reef," CCA Florida Executive Director Brian Gorski said in a statement.

Wanted in over 30 heinous criminal cases, carried ₹5 lakh reward: Punjab gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi brought back to India
He is accused of directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal networks in Punjab while operating from abroad.
Gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi, wanted in more than 30 heinous criminal cases, was brought to India from Ethiopia by the Punjab Police on Sunday. Police sources told HT that this was the first time the Punjab Police had secured the return of a fugitive from an African country.
Afridi, a resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, carried a ₹5 lakh reward announced by the Punjab government. Officials said he was taken into custody by the state police at Delhi airport during the intervening night of November 7 and 8 and was being brought to Punjab to face legal proceedings.
Who is gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi?
An alleged key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, he is accused of directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal networks in Punjab while operating from abroad, news agency PTI reported.
He is reportedly wanted in more than 30 serious criminal cases, including five murder cases, attempted murder, extortion and offences under the Arms Act.
His name surfaced during the investigation into an attack on a church in Thakkarpura village of Tarn Taran on August 31, 2022. Four masked men allegedly held the church's security guard at gunpoint, damaged statues of Lord Jesus and Mother Mary, and set the pastor's car on fire before escaping.
In June 2024, Amritsar Rural Police arrested Jaswinder Singh, alias Munshi, describing him as a key accused in the case. During his initial questioning, Munshi allegedly identified Afridi and two others as his associates in the attack, HT had reported earlier. Police then began searching for the remaining suspects.
Police have linked Afridi to five high-profile murders in Punjab. These include the killings of Sarpanch Rajwinder, alias Raj Talwandi, in October 2024; a 12-year-old in March 2025; Vicky Chugh in March 2025; Jaswant Singh in May 2025; and Congress block president Gurmel Singh in September 2025.
How he was caught
Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said Afridi left India from Mumbai airport for the UAE on March 31, 2025. He allegedly travelled using a fake passport obtained with the details of a resident of Gorakhpur. The passport was issued in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on February 12, 2025.
"The accused was constantly evading law enforcement agencies across several continents," Yadav said. He added that Afridi initially stayed in the UAE before attempting to reach Mexico through Istanbul. However, he was deported to the UAE.
Afridi later entered Kenya in April 2026, travelled to Angola in June 2026 and moved to Ethiopia in November 2026, where he was eventually arrested.
Yadav said the Punjab Police had secured an Interpol Red Notice against Afridi and regularly shared information about his false identity and movements with central agencies.
“This marks the successful culmination of ‘Operation SHAHID’, a 10-month-long intelligence-led international manhunt involving sustained surveillance, strategic intelligence gathering and tracking across multiple countries in Asia, South America and Africa, executed in close coordination with national and international agencies," he said.
Operation SHAHID was carried out under the supervision of Ashish Chaudhary, IGP (Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell or OFTEC) of the Counter Intelligence wing, who oversaw international coordination and follow-up efforts. The operation was led by Bikramjit Singh Brar, SP (Anti-Gangster Task Force/OFTEC OPs).
(Inputs from Ravinder Vasudeva and PTI)

On 4 November 2026, the results of the 2026 US midterm elections were announced, with the Democratic Party winning a majority in the House of Representatives & the Senate. Against this background, a video is being widely shared on social media (here, here, here) with the claim that it shows US President Donald Trump destroying his office following the Republican Party’s defeat in the 2026 US midterm elections. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Visuals showing US President Trump vandalizing his office after the Republican Party’s defeat in the midterm elections of 2026.
Fact: We found no credible reports confirming such an incident. This is an AI-generated video by a creator named Iman Rus. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
We found no credible reports confirming such an incident. A reverse image search using keyframes led us to the original video, which was uploaded on 4 November 2026 by the Iranian Embassy in Lebanon on X. The video clearly carries the label “AI Generated” in the upper-right corner. It also credits the creator, Iman Rus, at the end.
A keyword search based on the information gathered above led us to the same video uploaded on the YouTube channel ‘Iman Rus’ on 4 November 2026. The video title clearly identifies it as AI-generated. Additionally, YouTube’s AI disclosure in the video also confirms that the content was created using AI.
We also analysed the viral video using AI detection tools, Hive AI and SynthID, both of which indicated the video was AI-generated.
To sum up, the viral video claiming that Trump vandalised his office following the Republican Party’s defeat is AI-generated.

There may be 200-300 people at National’s event in Auckland, but the mood is muted, with long stretches of near-silence as the results roll in.
National may scoop up more seats than Labour via an overhang – enough to nudge the coalition back into power. But the results are still precarious. A higher number of National-leaning seats have been counted early, with some Labour strongholds still to come through. Meanwhile, a number of National’s high profile MPs are at risk of not making it back into parliament on the list.
No one here is in celebration mode yet with the vote so tight.
Keep an eye on the inner Auckland suburb of Mt Albert.
It’s been held by two Labour prime ministers, Helen Clark and Jacinda Ardern, but Labour’s Helen White won it by only 20 votes in 2023.
This year, the Greens have been pushing hard as has Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong. That had Labour worried about a potential vote split allowing National’s Melissa Lee to come through the middle and claim the seat.
But so far, with 13% counted, White is ahead of Lee by 465 votes.
Who is the Opportunity Party, this year’s potential kingmaker?
Eva Corlett
Who is the Opportunity Party, this year’s potential kingmaker?
Opinion polls in the lead up the election showed the Opportunity party, led by businesswoman Qiulae Wong, 38, clearing the 5% threshold to become kingmaker.
The centrist minor party, whose policies include a land tax and a $370 a week universal basic income, says it is looking to “market-driven solutions” while being committed to a low-emission future and evidence-based policy.
Opportunity will negotiate first with the party that secures the highest number of votes.
However, Luxon has ruled out working with Opportunity numerous times, saying its proposed land tax runs contrary to National’s “no new taxes” pledge.
The media outlet Stuff, which is hosting a panel of pundits, has just said it is looking like Opportunity could hold the balance of power by the end of the night, given how things are currently trending.
For anyone tuning in who needs a refresher on the MMP electoral system, here goes:
MMP means voters are asked to vote twice – once for their preferred party and the second time for an electorate MP.
There is a single chamber of parliament which generally has 120 MPs. This is the overhang issue which I think we’re going to be talking about tonight as results come in.
Under MMP it is very uncommon for a single party to form a government.
If there is no majority winner, the major parties will start negotiations after the election and can either form a coalition or confidence-and-supply agreements with minor parties. The party with the largest number of votes does not necessarily win, and negotiations can take days or weeks.
Some senior National heavy hitters will, remarkably, be out of a job if National’s party vote goes badly tonight.
Those most at risk include:
Nicola Willis (finance minister), Chris Bishop (like Willis, is tipped as a potential future leader of the party), Paul Goldsmith (justice minister) and Gerry Brownlee (speaker of the house).
Some background: All the pre-election polls looked bad for any National MP who was relying on the list vote to return them to parliament; such as Willis and Brownlee, who are list-only candidates. Goldsmith (Epsom) and Bishop (Hutt South) are both engaged in tense, marginal electorate battles. If either loses, they are then reliant on winning via the list. We’ll be watching all this closely.
Some of the Labour party candidates are locked in neck and neck races, with tensions high for those at the Labour party event watching the candidates in Hutt South. With more than 20% of the vote counted, Labour’s Ginny Anderson has edged just ahead of the incumbent, National MP Chris Bishop, by just a handful of ballots.
Green MP Julie-Anne Genter is just holding off Labour challenger Craig Renney in Wellington North, while Labour’s Kieran McAnulty is winning against National’s Mike Butterick in Wairarapa.
Elsewhere in Wellington, Labour party MP Ayesha Verrall was hoping to win Wellington North off the incumbent Green MP Tamatha Paul, but early votes suggest this won’t be the case. Paul is leading comfortably, at almost twice Verrall’s count in an electorate where Green is also leading the party vote.
Another key feature of this election has been the possibility of an overhang - where a party wins more electorates than its share of the party vote.
If that occurs, more seats will be added to parliament to make up the difference and could dictate which coalition can form a government.
Te Pāti Māori (the Māori party) has been calling on supporters to engineer an overhang for its party - by voting for its candidates in the Māori seats, and not giving them a party vote. This could benefit the left bloc.
Meanwhile, if National holds on to a good portion of its seats but its party vote falls short, that will give the party an edge to form a government but could see some of its most prominent MPs out of parliament.
Elsewhere in the Upper Hutt Cosmopolitan Club, punters were ordering crate bottles of local beer Tui and listening to a band kick up a rendition of Tennessee Whiskey.
For Hutt locals, the Cossie Club is a social hub; karaoke on Thursdays, Bingo on Sundays, and a jug of lager for $14 during happy hour.
While everyone spoken to by The Guardian voted for Hipkins in the Remutaka electorate – “he’s a local boy,” – party votes were otherwise split between Labour, the Opportunity party, and NZ First.
“I’ve always voted Labour, Chris knows that,” said Gladys Cooney, 96. “I haven’t heard anything from them this election, I don’t think anyone has gone deep enough.” The cost of living was appalling, she said. “Everything you touch has gone up.”
Fellow local Paul O’Riley also voted for Hipkins, but party voted NZ First. “I worked for 50 years in this country as a truck driver, Winston [Peters] does the most for us.”
Seven of the seats in New Zealand’s 120-seat parliamentare Māori electorates. Voters of Māori descent can choose to vote on the Māori roll – allowing them to vote for these seats – or the general roll. More than half of Māori voters are on the Māori roll.
They still get two votes; one for the electorate, and one for their preferred political party.
Last election, Te Pāti Māori won six of the seven seats. But internal turmoil has plagued the party since. Tonight, eyes will be on Te Tai Tokerau – covering the geographical area from New Zealand’s most northern point in Cape Reinga to West Auckland – where the Green’s candidate Hūhana Lyndon could help the party nab their first Māori seat.
Latest polls put her leading the race, followed by Labour’s Willow-Jean Prime and Te Pāti Māori candidate Aperahama Edwards.
Te Pāti Māori remain ahead in most other electorates, aside from Ikaroa-Rāwhiti and Te Tai Tonga (the biggest electorate, covering the entirety of the South Island and Stewart Island) where Labour candidates lead polling.
In an election night that has come down to Chris vs Chris, it’s important to know the difference.
Christopher Luxon, 56, the incumbent, leader of the National party and PM since 2023, is the former chief executive of the country’s national airline, Air New Zealand, and previously worked a slew of corporate jobs worldwide. He entered parliament in 2020, winning the Auckland electorate of Botany. A father-of-two, he is Christian but doesn’t discuss his faith, and has emphasised his business credentials — in 2023, his party was elected on its economic pledges.
Chris Hipkins, 48, the career politician who leads the center-left Labour party, is having a second crack at being PM tonight. Following the resignation of Jacinda Ardern in January 2023, Hipkins, also a father of two, took the reins for nine months ahead of that election, which his party lost. He’s held the Remutaka electorate in parliament since 2008. Some voters still associate him with Covid-19 and strict lockdown measures, while others connect with his pledges for better healthcare and improved cost of living.
National party faithful are starting to trickle into its event at the cavernous Viaduct Event Centre on Auckland’s waterfront. The room is awash in blue light.
People are grabbing drinks and milling around. The reaction is flicking between nervousness and excitement as the first numbers show the race is - as predicted - neck and neck.
As the first results of the night flashed up onto the big screen, Labour party volunteer Jasmine, 22, who works in the public service and didn’t want to use her last name, stopped talking mid-sentence.
A hush fell over the room as the first poll results show the main parties neck and neck . “That’s close,” she said, exhaling. “It’s great that Opportunity is over 5%, I’m happy about that. It’s just overwhelming; this is years of work, and that’s real numbers.” She’s been working for the party since she was 16.
Cheers are going up in the room as electorate results begin to come in. About 200 party supporters are expected here tonight.

Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don’t agree on why.
In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate.
The missing electrons
Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there’s these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said.
Over the decades, physicists have put forward two main competing explanations. The first hypothesizes that the electrons get stuck in some sort of structure. In this view, electrons freeze into patterns, such as charge density waves, and superconductivity develops separately. The alternative explanation tightly links this phenomenon to superconductivity. “Other people think they’re missing because they form pairs,” Allan said. Pairs of electrons, called Cooper pairs, are what carry current in a superconductor. If, as the material cools, these pairs appear before the material becomes superconducting, they would be a precondition of superconductivity, a waiting room of sorts, where pairs exist but can’t yet move together in lockstep.
Settling this proved extremely hard. “Lots of different experimental signatures are kind of lumped inside this,” Allan said. Different instruments all see something, but their readings, Allan said, are never conclusive. “It’s always something kind of incoherent, hard to grasp,” he said. What the researchers needed was a way to see pairs directly, and Allan and his colleagues figured it out.

New Delhi, Nov 9: Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a telephonic conversation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday during which Modi conveyed India's readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict with Russia.
PM Modi also reaffirmed India's human-centric approach and reiterated India's consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.
The prime minister conveyed India's readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at the peaceful resolution of the conflict, a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.
During the telephonic conversation, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments related to the ongoing conflict.
The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors for the mutual benefit of the two peoples.
"Glad to have had a productive telephone conversation with President Zelenskyy. We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties," PM Modi said on X.
"I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace. Reiterated India’s firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution," he said.
In August, Zelenskyy said Kyiv was counting on "India's contribution to ending the war with Russia".

Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov has also said that India has declared its readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the Ukraine conflict and Russia is grateful to New Delhi for such readiness and the ideas.

YouTube will once again be part of Billboard chart calculations in 2027
Billboard will give more weight to free, ad-supported listening in its methodology.
Starting next year, YouTube performance will once again factor into where music places on the Billboard charts. The Google-owned platform opted to stop sharing its data with Billboard in December 2025, claiming that the charts didn't assign sufficient value to free, ad-supported listening in their calculations.
Performance on streaming platforms is included in the results of the Billboard 200 and Hot 100 charts, as well as in its album genre charts and multi-metric song charts, but Billboard has long weighted listens from paid subscribers over free ones. That policy still holds, but Billboard announced today that it will adjust the math regarding the margin between free and paid listens. Beginning in January 2027, the company will count 1,500 ad-supported streams as an album consumption unit, which is the equivalent of selling one album or getting 1,000 streams from paying listeners. Under Billboard's previous calculations, 2,500 ad-supported streams were required to make one album consumption unit.
As a result of these new equivalence rules, YouTube is now willing to share its data with the charting company again. The update to its previous announcement about withdrawing from Billboard's accounts simply states: "We are returning to the Billboard charts starting in 2027. Billboard's new methodology better reflects how fans engage with music today across both subscription and ad-supported services."

Blades Brown has become the youngest PGA Tour winner since 1931 after the 19-year-old came back from a deficit of seven shots with a nine-under 63 to defeat Ben James in the World Wide Technology Championship.

Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
- Published
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.
Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.
"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk."
After Nvidia's investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang to continue leading the firm.
US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened the week on a positive note after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.
But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so important to the AI industry.
"Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but he decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
Huang's position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses
A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Jensen Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
Jensen Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.
Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Jensen Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future."
The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched.
Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.

Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Jensen Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.

Welcome to Kernel Panic, a weekly newsletter by Lily Hay Newman and Matt Burgess from inside the new world of privacy and digital security. To receive this newsletter in your inbox each week, sign up here.
Amid an onslaught of AI vulnerability discovery and AI-assisted hacking, some of the most consequential critical infrastructure attacks this year may have little to do with the technology at all—instead providing a stark reminder that cybersecurity fundamentals are still key to digital defense.
Three sites in France that handle blood and plasma bags were briefly impacted this week by widespread attacks on vulnerable internet-connected refrigerators. On Wednesday, the Établissement Français du Sang (EFS) confirmed that cold rooms storing blood were “raised to very high temperatures” on November 2. The blood samples, thankfully, weren’t altered or damaged, the EFS said, because the organization’s alarm facilities and staff quickly detected the changes and implemented fail-safe measures.
The incident, however, comes amid a wave of cyberattacks in recent days affecting supermarket chains in at least 11 European countries that also drastically increased the temperatures of their refrigerators. Pictures from across the continent show huge volumes of food being trashed following the spikes. Similar fridge attacks in October affected hundreds of French stores that were forced to throw away food. And in August, roughly six commissaries and grocery stores on United States military bases suffered similar incidents resulting in spoiled food. The Pentagon is investigating the incidents and is collaborating with French law enforcement, Reuters reported last week.
“It's been true for more than a decade now that our dependence on connected technology is growing faster than our collective will to protect it, which has exposed us to accidents, adversaries, and now potentially agents,” says longtime critical infrastructure researcher Josh Corman, who is currently the executive in residence for public safety and resilience at the nonprofit Institute for Security and Technology. “These fragile cold-chain systems are too critical to fail, but we keep experiencing hard lessons.”
It is still unclear who is behind the incidents and whether the attacks are all connected or being carried out by multiple actors. The first recent wave of attacks against French supermarkets last month appears to have been caused by attackers exploiting unpatched refrigeration controllers exposed to the internet—including software versions that allegedly used weak passwords formulated based on the date.
Many of the hacks stem from attackers exploiting vulnerabilities in temperature controllers made by the Danish firm Danfoss, and researchers say the attacks would not have been particularly difficult to pull off. Danfoss did not return WIRED’s request for comment.
In other statements, Danfoss said impacted systems “were running outdated firmware” and urged customers to keep products updated. In an alert on Thursday addressing the rash of incidents, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said attacks could exploit flaws in cold storage systems via authentication bypasses, arbitrary code injections, and weak configurations. Experts have long warned about the dire threats to critical infrastructure posed by these types of weaknesses in so-called internet-of-things devices.
Russian hacktivists tried to claim responsibility for some of the attacks but did not provide credible evidence. Still, some researchers see signs that Russia-based actors may have been involved in at least some of the incidents. The Kremlin this week denied involvement. In other cases, researchers have found potential ties to Iran-linked actors. NextGov/FCW reported last week that unnamed US officials suspect Iran-linked attackers may have been behind the freezer attacks on US military bases, though they noted that the investigation is still ongoing.
This type of refrigerator/freezer attack is not new. Back in 2022, 16 supermarkets in Russia were targeted at the start of the country’s full-scale war with Ukraine. That year, 40 stores in Israel were similarly attacked, according to a 2025 report by Danfoss.
“Many businesses use older technology while the systems become increasingly connected,” Sweden’s National Cyber Security Center pointed out in a recent advisory about the freezer attacks, noting that companies should inventory which of their devices are connected to the internet, disconnect them whenever possible, and make sure they are kept access-controlled, patched, and monitored if they must be connected.
